```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 150)
# --- User switches -----------------------------------------------------------
# RUN_ATTRITION: TRUE renders the full sample-attrition section (funnel figure,
# per-modality retention table, stage notes) from data/qc/attrition/. FALSE
# skips the attrition logs entirely and prints only the starting and final
# sample counts (the N_* constants below and the data-driven mapping N).
RUN_ATTRITION <- TRUE
N_STARTING_LIBRARIES <- 606  # RNA-seq libraries in the cohort metadata
N_QUANTIFIED         <- 605  # Salmon-quantified (SRR13696952 never quantified)
source(params$module_path)
dir.create(params$fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(params$table_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
# gene_map.tsv is regenerated in full from the normalized GTF by
# make_report_archive.sh — every tested gene has a symbol entry.
gene_map <- read_tsv(params$gene_map_path, col_types = "cccc", progress = FALSE)
sym <- function(ids) gene_map$symbol[match(ids, gene_map$gene_id)]
# display symbol: fall back to the gene ID when the GTF has no gene_name
symd <- function(ids) ifelse(is.na(sym(ids)) | sym(ids) == "", ids, sym(ids))
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
```

```{r load-data}
grouped   <- load_layer(params$data_dir, "grouped")
ungrouped <- load_layer(params$data_dir, "ungrouped")
combined  <- load_layer(params$data_dir, "combined") %>% driver_modality()
# stepwise (independent) outputs: grouped + combined + ungrouped layers,
# rows tagged by `layer`
independent <- load_independent(params$data_dir)

# QC input paths (used by the cohort-landscape sections)
qc_in <- file.path(params$qc_dir, "qtl_inputs")
qc_pc <- file.path(params$qc_dir, "genotype_pcs")

# Sample sizes: ground truth from the final covariate tables (columns =
# post-intersection, post-outlier individuals as mapped). The full
# raw-to-mapping funnel is in the Sample attrition section.
n_samp <- sapply(c("EAS", "EUR"), function(a) {
  f <- file.path(qc_in, paste0(a, "_covariates.tsv"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NA_integer_)
  ncol(read_tsv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_double(),
                                    covariate_id = col_character()),
                progress = FALSE, n_max = 1)) - 1L
})
n_samp <- n_samp[c("EAS", "EUR")]
# Modality-level sample-size variation (a few samples per layer, from
# modality-specific harmonization) — descriptive range from the
# allele-count/frequency denominators.
n_range <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(ancestry, layer, modality) %>%
  summarise(n = round(median(ma_count / (2 * af))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(n_min = min(n), n_max = max(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tibble::deframe()

# Sample-attrition log (raw FASTQ -> QTL mapping), written by
# make_report_archive.sh — only read when the attrition section is rendered.
if (RUN_ATTRITION) {
  attr_dir <- file.path(params$qc_dir, "attrition")
  attr_samples <- read_tsv(file.path(attr_dir, "attrition_samples.tsv"),
                           col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                           progress = FALSE)
  attr_summary <- read_tsv(file.path(attr_dir, "attrition_summary.tsv"),
                           progress = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE)
  # Archives written before the dual-level schema lack `level`; treat their
  # counts as run-level and reuse them for the individual-level slots.
  if (!"level" %in% names(attr_summary)) attr_summary$level <- "run"
}

# Cross-ancestry concordance of the combined layer (referenced in the
# executive summary; the full per-modality table is in Cross-ancestry
# regulation)
dedup_best <- function(df) df %>% group_by(gene_id) %>%
  slice_min(pval_beta, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
conc_comb <- cross_ancestry_concordance(
  combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>% dedup_best(),
  combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EUR") %>% dedup_best())

# ---- DevBrain-style panel inputs (35_extract_report_extras.py) ------------
# All optional: each downstream panel renders only when its file is present.
extras_dir <- file.path(dirname(params$data_dir), "extras")
read_extra <- function(fname, ...) {
  f <- file.path(extras_dir, fname)
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  read_tsv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), progress = FALSE, ...)
}
xanc_lookup <- read_extra("cross_ancestry_lookup.tsv.gz") %>%
  {if (is.null(.)) NULL else mutate(., across(c(repl_slope, repl_se, repl_pval,
                                                discovery_slope, discovery_qval),
                                              as.numeric))}
xmod_lookup <- read_extra("cross_modality_lookup.tsv.gz") %>%
  {if (is.null(.)) NULL else mutate(., across(c(repl_slope, repl_se, repl_pval),
                                              as.numeric))}
lead_annot <- read_extra("lead_variant_annotations.tsv.gz") %>%
  {if (is.null(.)) NULL else mutate(., pos = as.numeric(pos))}
constraint <- read_extra("gene_constraint.tsv") %>%
  {if (is.null(.)) NULL else mutate(., across(c(pLI, oe_lof, oe_lof_upper, lof_z),
                                              as.numeric))}
pcair_pcs <- read_extra("pcair_pcs.tsv") %>%
  {if (is.null(.)) NULL else mutate(., across(starts_with("PC"), as.numeric))}
finemap_loci <- read_extra("finemap_locus_summary.tsv") %>%
  {if (is.null(.)) NULL else
    mutate(., across(c(n_cs_out, max_pip), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.))))}
finemap_cs <- read_extra("finemap_credible_sets.tsv.gz") %>%
  {if (is.null(.)) NULL else
    mutate(., across(c(n_variants, lead_pip, mean_pip, min_pip, cs_start,
                       cs_end), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))) %>%
      mutate(across(ends_with("_est_corr"), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.))))}
locus_files <- if (dir.exists(extras_dir))
  list.files(extras_dir, pattern = "^locus_.*_(EAS|EUR)\\.tsv\\.gz$",
             full.names = TRUE) else character(0)
locus_scans <- if (length(locus_files) > 0)
  bind_rows(lapply(locus_files, function(f)
    read_tsv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), progress = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(across(c(pos, repl_slope, repl_se, repl_pval, r2_lead), as.numeric)))) else NULL
# gene bodies for the locus-track gene-model panels (archive data/)
gene_bodies <- if (file.exists(params$gene_bodies_path))
  read_tsv(params$gene_bodies_path,
           col_types = cols(gene_id = col_character(), chr = col_character(),
                            start = col_double(), end = col_double(),
                            strand = col_double()),
           progress = FALSE) else NULL
```

# Executive summary

```{r exec-numbers}
fdr <- 0.05
n_cells <- nrow(bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
                  distinct(layer, ancestry, modality))
yield <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(layer, ancestry, modality) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), fdr05 = sum(qval <= fdr), fdr10 = sum(qval <= 0.10),
            min_q = min(qval), .groups = "drop")
n_fdr05 <- sum(yield$fdr05)  # total FDR ≤ 5% rows across ALL layers

# Discovery layer of record: the ungrouped phenotype-level scan for the 8
# multi-phenotype modalities plus the primary per-gene scan for expression
# (expression has one phenotype per gene, so its grouped scan IS the
# phenotype-level scan). This is the set carried into SuSHiE fine-mapping.
xpheno <- bind_rows(ungrouped,
                    grouped %>% filter(modality == "expression"))
xpheno_hits <- xpheno %>% filter(qval <= fdr)
n_xp <- xpheno_hits %>% count(ancestry, name = "n") %>% tibble::deframe()
n_xp <- n_xp[c("EAS", "EUR")]; n_xp[is.na(n_xp)] <- 0L
n_xp_genes <- xpheno_hits %>% distinct(ancestry, gene_id) %>%
  count(ancestry, name = "n") %>% tibble::deframe()
n_xp_genes <- n_xp_genes[c("EAS", "EUR")]; n_xp_genes[is.na(n_xp_genes)] <- 0L

# Gene-level rollups: combined cross-modality layer (primary gene catalog)
# with per-modality grouped eGenes as the breakdown.
hits <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>% filter(qval <= fdr)
egenes_combined <- combined %>% filter(qval <= fdr)
egenes_grouped  <- grouped %>% filter(qval <= fdr)
n_eg <- egenes_combined %>% count(ancestry, name = "n") %>% tibble::deframe()
n_eg <- n_eg[c("EAS", "EUR")]; n_eg[is.na(n_eg)] <- 0L
n_eg_mod <- egenes_grouped %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "n")

# top association overall + per ancestry (for the headline)
top_hit <- bind_rows(grouped, combined, ungrouped) %>%
  slice_min(qval, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
top_by_anc <- bind_rows(grouped, combined, ungrouped) %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>% slice_min(qval, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()

# carrier-count audit (MAC >= 5 floor baked into the genotype intersection
# at module 23 — verify it propagated to the mapping outputs)
mac_audit <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(min_carriers = min(ma_count), n_lt5 = sum(ma_count < 5),
            .groups = "drop")

# short inline helpers for data-driven prose
fmt_genes <- function(ids) paste0("_", symd(ids), "_", collapse = ", ")
describe_hit <- function(h) {
  sprintf("%s (%s, %s layer, q = %s)", symd(h$gene_id), h$modality, h$layer,
          signif(h$qval, 2))
}
```

This report summarizes the multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis:
cohort-only genotype PCA on LD-pruned variants within each ancestry stratum,
a conventional covariate set (first 5 genotype PCs + HCP factors + sex,
gestational age, and cell-type fractions; maternal cell fraction excluded
before correlation pruning at |r| > 0.9; HCP count optimized per ancestry × modality
via module 25b; no covariate cap), a MAF ≥ 0.01 filter with a ≥ 5
minor-allele-count floor at the
genotype intersection, Storey q-values (computed with the R `qvalue`
package), and per-phenotype rank-based inverse-normal transformation of all
modalities (isoform usage mapped as within-gene relative-abundance ratios;
isoform expression as transcript-level TPM abundance).
Mapping covers
`r n_cells` ancestry × modality × layer cells (EAS n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`,
EUR n ≈ `r n_samp["EUR"]`). The results narrative follows the figure
progression of the developing-brain xQTL atlas (Wen et al., Science 2024):
cohort landscape → calibration → the modality-wise regulation landscape →
cross-ancestry regulation → the discovery catalog → functional
characterization.

```{r exec-pi1}
pi1_cells <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(layer, ancestry, modality) %>%
  summarise(pi1 = storey_pi1(pval_beta), .groups = "drop")
pi1_range <- range(pi1_cells$pi1, na.rm = TRUE)
hit_r2 <- if (nrow(hits) > 0) range(approx_r2(hits$slope, hits$af)) else NULL
# genomic-control lambda on the EAS splicing layer (referenced in the prose)
lambda_eas_splicing <- (grouped %>%
  filter(ancestry == "EAS", modality == "splicing") %>%
  summarise(l = median(qchisq(1 - pval_beta, 1), na.rm = TRUE) /
              qchisq(0.5, 1), .groups = "drop"))$l
```

**Headline result: `r sum(n_xp)` phenotype-level associations reach FDR ≤ 5%**
in the discovery layer (ungrouped scan for the 8 multi-phenotype modalities +
the per-gene expression scan): `r n_xp["EAS"]` in EAS and `r n_xp["EUR"]` in
EUR, implicating `r n_xp_genes["EAS"]` / `r n_xp_genes["EUR"]` unique genes
respectively. This phenotype-level set is the input to cross-ancestry SuSHiE
fine-mapping (Methods). At gene level, the combined cross-modality catalog
contains **`r n_eg["EAS"]` EAS and `r n_eg["EUR"]` EUR eGenes** at FDR ≤ 5%,
with per-modality grouped eGenes as the breakdown. Strongest association per
ancestry:
`r paste(sprintf("%s: %s", top_by_anc$ancestry, apply(top_by_anc, 1, function(r) sprintf("%s (%s, %s layer, q = %s)", symd(r[["gene_id"]]), r[["modality"]], r[["layer"]], signif(as.numeric(r[["qval"]]), 2)))), collapse = "; ")`.
Storey calibration estimates a signal fraction (π1) of
`r round(100 * pi1_range[1])`–`r round(100 * pi1_range[2])`% across cells.
`r if (pi1_range[2] <= 0.05) "At these fractions Storey q-values are numerically close to Benjamini–Hochberg (Calibration)." else "In high-signal cells Storey q-values are correspondingly more liberal than Benjamini–Hochberg (by up to the estimated π0); the per-cell comparison is in Calibration."`

The splicing modality splits by ancestry. At its modality-matched HCP count
(HCP count optimization), EUR splicing yields
`r n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EUR" & n_eg_mod$modality == "splicing"]`
FDR ≤ 5% eGenes — under expression-derived covariates the layer carried no
detectable signal, so the EUR splicing null was a covariate-specification
artifact, now resolved. EAS splicing remains near-null in both the grouped
(`r n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EAS" & n_eg_mod$modality == "splicing"]`
eGenes, best q =
`r signif(min((grouped %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS", modality == "splicing"))$qval), 2)`)
and ungrouped
(`r sum(xpheno_hits$ancestry == "EAS" & xpheno_hits$modality == "splicing")`
phenotype-level hits) layers, its eGene yield is flat across the HCP grid,
and its p-values depart only mildly from the null at the median
(genomic-control λ = `r round(lambda_eas_splicing, 2)`; Calibration). Three
lines of evidence bear on the residual EAS null:

1. **The machinery detects splicing signal where it exists** — the same
   pipeline and covariate machinery yield the EUR splicing catalog above at
   n ≈ `r n_samp["EUR"]`, a *higher* detection floor (r² ≈ 0.19) than EAS
   (r² ≈ 0.10 at n = `r n_samp["EAS"]`; Power analysis). A pure
   sample-power explanation is therefore insufficient for EAS: EUR splicing
   effects cleared a higher bar. The leading candidate is EAS-specific
   attenuation of the splicing phenotypes — EAS pools four cohorts spanning
   single- and paired-end protocols, and junction-level quantification is
   the most protocol-sensitive of the nine modalities.
2. **The EAS null is not a covariate artifact** — eGene yield does not
   improve at any HCP count on the grid (HCP count optimization), and the
   mild median λ elevation with only a handful of FDR-significant hits is
   the signature of diffuse, individually weak effects rather than of
   residual confounding (which would inflate the median without bound) or
   of a dead layer (λ ≈ 1, no tail).
   `r if (!is.null(hit_r2)) sprintf("The FDR-significant hits in the other modalities carry estimated r² of %.2f–%.2f — exactly the class of outsize effect the floor permits.", hit_r2[1], hit_r2[2])`
3. **Signal replicates across ancestries** — cross-ancestry rank
   concordance of gene-level signal on the combined layer is Spearman ρ =
   `r round(conc_comb$rank_spearman, 2)` (top-100 overlap
   `r conc_comb$top100_overlap`/100), with same-variant slope concordance
   `r round(conc_comb$slope_spearman, 2)` — the pattern expected of real,
   partially shared genetic regulation, not of artifact-driven signal.

`r if (all(mac_audit$n_lt5 == 0)) sprintf("**Carrier-count audit: clean.** The MAC ≥ 5 floor (applied at the genotype intersection in module 23) propagated to every mapping output — minimum minor-allele carrier count across all tested pairs is %d (EAS) and %d (EUR).", mac_audit$min_carriers[mac_audit$ancestry == "EAS"], mac_audit$min_carriers[mac_audit$ancestry == "EUR"]) else sprintf("**Carrier-count caveat.** A fraction of tested pairs retain < 5 minor-allele carriers in the mapping sample sets (EAS: %d tests; EUR: %d tests; audit table below) — the MAC ≥ 5 floor was applied before outlier exclusion. Flagged tests should be discounted; no FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited.", mac_audit$n_lt5[mac_audit$ancestry == "EAS"], mac_audit$n_lt5[mac_audit$ancestry == "EUR"])`
# Methods

*Adapted from the project methods document (methods_placenta_xqtl.docx).*

## Study cohorts and data

Placental RNA-seq and genotype data were assembled from four cohorts (Table 1). NIEHS_RICHS contributed placenta RNA-seq and array genotypes under dbGaP controlled access. GUSTO contributed placenta RNA-seq and array genotypes through the study investigators. SNUH contributed placenta RNA-seq and genotypes available under SRA BioProject PRJNA820329 (102 RNA-seq runs). NIGMS contributed placenta RNA-seq and whole-exome sequencing (WXS) under SRA BioProject PRJNA671171 (154 RNA-seq runs and 95 WXS runs); each NIGMS subject was sampled at two placental sites, and the replicate libraries were averaged per individual before mapping. All genotype and transcriptomic data were processed against the GRCh38 no-alt analysis set (GCA_000001405.15).

| Cohort | Data types | Access | Accession / route |
|---|---|---|---|
| NIEHS_RICHS | Placenta RNA-seq, array genotypes | Controlled access | dbGaP (accession to be added on publication) |
| GUSTO | Placenta RNA-seq, array genotypes | On request | GUSTO study investigators |
| SNUH | Placenta RNA-seq, genotypes | Public | SRA BioProject PRJNA820329 |
| NIGMS | Placenta RNA-seq (2 sampling sites per subject), WXS | Public | SRA BioProject PRJNA671171 |

Table 1. Study cohorts, data types, and access routes.

## Genotype processing and imputation

Array genotypes were lifted over to GRCh38 where required. For NIGMS, WXS reads were retrieved from SRA, aligned to GRCh38 with BWA, processed to per-sample gVCFs with GATK, and jointly genotyped per chromosome. Each cohort was filtered before imputation to biallelic SNPs with per-variant missingness of at most 0.05, minor allele frequency (MAF) of at least 0.01, and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE) test P above 1 x 10^-6, and variants were left-aligned and normalized against the reference genome with bcftools norm. Genotypes were imputed on either the TOPMed (NIGMS, NIEHS_RICHS) or SEAD (GUSTO, SNUH) imputation servers. Imputed variants with imputation Rsq of at least 0.4 were retained and converted to plink2 binary format (pgen).

## Ancestry assignment and cross-cohort genotype pooling

Genetic ancestry was assigned within each cohort with PC-AiR as implemented in GENESIS, using kinship estimated with KING in SNPRelate and 1000 Genomes phase 3 samples as the unrelated reference set. Each sample was assigned to one of five continental ancestry strata (AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, SAS). For each stratum, the Rsq-passing variants of each cohort were subset to the assigned samples, multiallelic sites were split per cohort so that imputed dosages were partitioned correctly, and cohort VCFs were merged across cohorts with bcftools merge and normalized against GRCh38. Pooled genotypes were filtered to MAF of at least 0.01, HWE P above 1 x 10^-6, and per-variant missingness of at most 0.05, and palindromic duplicate sites were removed. The resulting per-ancestry pgen files define the genotype identifier space used by all downstream steps.

## RNA-seq processing

RNA-seq reads for SNUH and NIGMS were retrieved from SRA with prefetch and fasterq-dump; GUSTO and NIEHS_RICHS FASTQs were already local. Adapters and low-quality bases were trimmed with Trim Galore 0.6.10. Reads were aligned to GRCh38 with STAR 2.7.4a in basic two-pass mode. Transcript abundance was quantified with Salmon 1.10.2 against the HPLRv2 long-read placental transcriptome annotation using automatic library-type detection, selective alignment with validateMappings, and 20 bootstrap replicates per sample.

## Transcriptomic phenotyping

Nine RNA modalities were quantified per sample with an in-house rewrite of the PANTRY phenotyping pipeline (github.com/PejLab/Pantry) adapted to the local compute cluster. Gene expression was taken as gene-level abundance aggregated from Salmon with tximport. Isoform expression was taken as transcript-level TPM after quantification uncertainty correction (see below). Isoform usage was computed as within-gene relative abundance ratios after correcting transcript counts for quantification uncertainty: edgeR catchSalmon was used to estimate per-transcript overdispersion from the Salmon bootstrap replicates, and counts were divided by the estimated overdispersion (Chen et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2023). Alternative transcription start site and alternative polyadenylation usage were quantified with txrevise: event annotations were constructed in two event groups, each split into upstream, contained, and downstream positional classes, and event abundance was quantified with Salmon against the six resulting transcript indices. Splice junction usage was quantified by extracting junctions from the STAR alignments with RegTools and clustering them with leafCutter (minimum 30 reads per cluster, minimum cluster ratio 0.001); intron usage ratios within clusters were carried as phenotypes. Intron retention was quantified with MAJIQ. RNA editing levels were computed at REDIportal sites (TABLE1_hg38_v3) from samtools mpileup output as the proportion of edited reads per site. RNA stability was approximated per gene as the ratio of exonic to intronic read counts from featureCounts. Because splice junctions and retained introns are defined by the observed data in each cohort, splicing and intron retention features were harmonized across cohorts by stable genomic coordinates before pooling. Phenotypes were exported as bgzipped, tabix-indexed BED files with gene-level phenotype groupings where applicable.

## Cell-type deconvolution

Cell-type proportions were estimated from bulk gene expression with MuSiC, using a published placental single-cell RNA-seq reference (GSE182381). The estimated fractions were carried into the mapping covariates.

## RNA to DNA sample linkage

RNA-seq sample identifiers were linked to genotype sample identifiers within each cohort using cohort-specific keys: SRA run-to-subject metadata for SNUH and NIGMS, and array subject identifiers for NIEHS_RICHS and GUSTO. The linkage table was checked for match rates, duplicates, and missing values before mapping.

## Phenotype pooling, normalization, and batch correction

Within each ancestry stratum, per-cohort phenotype matrices were pooled and normalized in a single pass, following the conventions of the developing-brain xQTL atlas (Wen et al., Science 2024). Gene and isoform expression were filtered to features with TPM above 0.1 in more than 25% of samples, and ratio-based modalities were filtered to features detected in at least 40% of samples. Filtered matrices were quantile normalized, and each phenotype was rank inverse-normal transformed. For expression, sample outliers were removed before batch correction using signed bicor network connectivity (z below -3). Cross-cohort batch effects were adjusted with ComBat (sva) with cohort as the batch variable, applied as the final normalization step.

## Genotype principal components and sample quality control

Within each stratum, pooled genotypes were LD-pruned (plink2 indep-pairwise 200 50 0.2) and 20 principal components (PCs) were computed exactly; the first five PCs were retained as covariates. Genotype and phenotype sample sets were intersected on the linkage map, and variants were further required to have a minor allele count of at least 5 in the intersected samples. Samples more than 6 standard deviations from the mean on any of the first five genotype PCs were excluded.

## Covariate assembly and hidden factor estimation

Mapping covariates comprised the first five genotype PCs, sex, gestational age, estimated cell-type fractions (with the dominant cell type as the compositional reference and the maternal fraction excluded), and hidden confounding factors estimated from batch-corrected expression with Rhcpp, using Picard alignment quality-control metrics as known covariates. Covariates with near-zero variance were dropped, and the remaining set was pruned iteratively at pairwise absolute correlation above 0.9, with retention priority given to sex and gestational age, then genotype PCs, then cell types, then hidden factors. The number of hidden factors was optimized separately for each ancestry and modality: factors were re-estimated at each k in {0...5...100} by 5, chromosome 1 was mapped with tensorQTL under each candidate covariate set (the full genome was mapped for modalities with fewer than 300 chromosome-1 phenotypes), and the k yielding the most eGenes at Storey q of at most 0.05 was selected, with ties resolved to the smaller k.

## cis-xQTL mapping

cis-QTL mapping was performed per ancestry stratum and modality with tensorQTL 1.0.10 under GTEx conventions: a cis window of 1 Mb on either side of the phenotype start, MAF of at least 0.01, nominal and permutation passes, and Storey q-values computed on the permutation beta-approximated P values with the R qvalue package. For modalities with gene-level phenotype groupings, grouped permutation (group_s) was used to select one lead variant per gene; the remaining modalities were mapped ungrouped. Multiple independent signals per gene (grouped layers) or per phenotype (ungrouped layer) were identified with the stepwise conditional mode (map_independent). Three result layers were produced per ancestry: grouped, ungrouped, and a combined cross-modality layer in which phenotype identifiers are namespaced by modality.

## Cross-ancestry fine-mapping

FDR-significant lead phenotypes (q of at most 0.05) were pooled across ancestries per modality — from the primary per-gene scan for expression and from the ungrouped phenotype-level scan for all other modalities — and each locus was fine-mapped jointly across ancestries with SuSHiE (version 0.20 or later) in individual-level mode, using in-sample linkage disequilibrium from the intersected genotypes and the exact tested cis windows. The number of effects per locus was set to min(10, max(5, n_independent + 2)), where n_independent is the number of stepwise-conditional signals at the locus, and credible sets were filtered at a purity threshold of 0.5. Per-variant posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs), credible-set membership, per-ancestry effect weights, and the cross-ancestry effect-size correlation were recorded for each locus.

## Functional enrichment of fine-mapped variants

High-confidence variants (PIP of at least 0.9) were compared against all fine-mapped variants for enrichment in functional annotations. Variant consequences were annotated with fastVEP (GRCh38) and grouped into splice, loss-of-function, missense, synonymous, UTR, intron, regulatory, flanking, and intergenic classes. Regulatory annotations comprised ENCODE SCREEN candidate cis-regulatory element classes and placenta open-chromatin regions. Enrichment was tested with Fisher exact tests as the primary analysis, logistic regression adjusting for log10 distance to the transcription start site as a sensitivity analysis, and PIP-weighted enrichment; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR was applied within each test family.

## Report-integration targeted lookups

To support cross-ancestry and cross-modality report panels without shipping genome-wide summary statistics, targeted association lookups were performed (script 35): for each FDR-significant lead (variant, phenotype) pair, the same pair's slope, standard error, and nominal P value were recomputed in the other ancestry stratum and, for grouped-layer leads, across the gene's phenotypes in every other modality within the same ancestry, by ordinary least squares on covariate-residualized genotypes and phenotypes. All unique lead variants were annotated with fastVEP consequence classes and intersected with ENCODE cCRE classes and placenta open-chromatin regions, and per-gene loss-of-function constraint metrics (pLI, LOEUF) were taken from gnomAD v2.1.1. Regional association scans (plus-minus 1 Mb) with linkage disequilibrium (r^2) to the lead variant were computed for two showcase loci (ERAP2 and the top shared non-expression-driver locus).

## Software and computing

All pipeline stages were run on the MD Anderson seadragon high-performance computing cluster (LSF scheduler, RHEL8). Analyses used R 4.3.1 (GENESIS, GWASTools, SNPRelate, sva, Rhcpp, edgeR, tximport, rtracklayer, MuSiC, qvalue, data.table) and Python 3 (tensorqtl 1.0.10, sushie, pandas, pyarrow, genotypeio). The complete analysis codebase, including per-stage scripts, configuration files, and a step-by-step manifest, is available at github.com/sbresnahan/Placenta_xQTL_atlas.

# Pipeline and calibration

*Processing pipeline and mapping calibration, in the style of DevBrain
Fig. S2 (pipeline) and Figs. S3/S5/S6 (per-modality mapping QC: HCP
optimization, permutation calibration, signal fraction).*

## Pipeline recap

- **Phenotypes**: 9 RNA modalities (gene expression, isoform usage, isoform
  expression, splice junction usage, intron retention, alternative TSS,
  alternative polyA, RNA editing, RNA stability), harmonized to genotyped
  samples (array_id), with NIGMS technical replicates averaged per
  individual. The two isoform modalities are both built from QU-corrected
  Salmon transcript counts (mean count ≥ 10): **isoform usage** is
  within-gene relative-abundance ratios (transcript TPM / gene-total TPM;
  PANTRY convention, mean ratio in [0.05, 0.95]) and **isoform expression**
  is the pre-ratio transcript TPM abundance (DevBrain §3.3 convention).
  Per ancestry stratum:
  feature filtering (isoform usage: usage > 0.1 in > 25% of samples;
  isoform expression: TPM > 0.1 in > 25% of samples, DevBrain
  §3.3; ratio modalities: detected in ≥ 40%, DevBrain §3.4),
  batch-median NA imputation, quantile normalization across samples +
  rank-based inverse-normal transformation per phenotype, then ComBat
  (batch = cohort) **last** — the DevBrain "ComBat on the normalized data"
  convention. No log2 pre-transform is applied: rank-based INT is invariant
  to any monotone transform, so log2/VST would be exact no-ops on the
  mapped scale.
- **Genotypes**: ancestry-stratified plink2 pgen; variants filtered to
  **MAF ≥ 0.01 with MAC ≥ 5** (≥ 5 minor alleles) at the genotype
  intersection — the count floor excludes low-carrier tests, which can
  produce spurious associations, while MAF 0.01 keeps the variant pool as
  large as defensible. tensorQTL's own MAF ≥ 0.01 filter applies on top at
  mapping time.
- **Genotype PCA**: cohort-only PCA per ancestry on LD-pruned variants
  (plink2 `--indep-pairwise 200 50 0.2`, then `--pca 20 exact`) — the GTEx
  convention.
- **Covariates**: per ancestry × modality, first-5 genotype PCs + HCP factors
  1–k\* (k\* selected per ancestry × modality by module 25b, chr1 eGene
  maximization on each modality's own HCPs) + sex + gestational
  age + cell-type fractions (Syncytiotrophoblast as reference). The maternal
  cell-fraction covariate (`ct_Maternal`) is excluded BEFORE pruning by
  analysis decision (coded `--exclude-covariates`); the remaining pool is correlation-pruned (iterative max-|r| >
  0.9 removal, protecting sex/GA > PCs > cell types > HCPs — correlated
  HCPs are dropped, so effective k can fall below nominal k\*) with **no
  covariate cap** (details and QC below).
- **Mapping** (tensorQTL, cis window ±1 Mb): (i) **per-modality grouped** —
  all phenotypes of a gene within a modality tested as one group
  (permutation-calibrated gene-level p-value; the row label is the
  *driver phenotype*); (ii) **combined** — all phenotypes of a gene across
  all modalities as one cross-modality group (PANTRY's headline design);
  (iii) **ungrouped** — per-phenotype lead variants for transcript-level
  resolution, and the discovery layer of record for fine-mapping;
  (iv) **stepwise** (`cis.map_independent`) for conditionally independent
  signals, entered at FDR ≤ 5% and run on the grouped, ungrouped, and
  combined layers alike.
- **Multiple testing**: **Storey q-values** on the
  permutation-calibrated p-value (pval_beta), computed with the R `qvalue`
  package (default lambda) — the GTEx convention, and statistically
  identical to tensorQTL's own `calculate_qvalues`. (On this cluster the
  rpy2/conda-R route to `qvalue` hits an unresolvable libstdc++/GLIBCXX
  conflict, so q-values are computed through a file-based bridge to the
  singularity R container used elsewhere in the pipeline.)

## HCP count optimization (module 25b)

```{r hcp-optimization, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
hcp_opt <- bind_rows(lapply(c("EAS", "EUR"), function(a) {
  lapply(c(MODALITY_LEVELS, "combined"), function(m) {
    f <- file.path(params$qc_dir, "hcp_optimization_modalities",
                   paste0(a, "_", m, "_optimal_hcp.tsv"))
    if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
    read_tsv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_double(),
                                 ancestry = col_character(),
                                 modality = col_character(),
                                 mapping_scope = col_character(),
                                 chosen = col_logical()),
             progress = FALSE)
  }) %>% bind_rows()
}))
if (nrow(hcp_opt) > 0) {
  hcp_opt <- hcp_opt %>%
    mutate(modality = factor(modality, levels = c(MODALITY_LEVELS, "combined")))
  k_star <- hcp_opt %>% filter(chosen) %>%
    select(ancestry, modality, k, n_egenes, n_tested, mapping_scope,
           n_hcp_used, n_hcp_dropped)
  p_hcp <- ggplot(hcp_opt, aes(k, n_egenes, color = ancestry)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    geom_point(data = hcp_opt %>% filter(chosen),
               shape = 21, size = 3, stroke = 1.2, fill = NA) +
    facet_wrap(~modality, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(EAS = "#0072B2", EUR = "#D55E00")) +
    labs(x = "HCP factors (k)", y = "eGenes (Storey q ≤ 0.05)") +
    theme_report() + theme(legend.position = "top")
  print(p_hcp)
  ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_hcp_optimization.png"), p_hcp,
         width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)
  knitr::kable(k_star %>% arrange(modality, ancestry) %>%
                 select(ancestry, modality, k, n_egenes, n_tested, mapping_scope),
               col.names = c("ancestry", "modality", "k*", "eGenes at k*",
                             "phenotypes tested", "mapping scope"),
               caption = "Chosen HCP count (k*) per ancestry × modality: argmax eGene yield, ties to the smaller k. Selection maps a chr1 phenotype subset, except modalities whose full phenotype set is too small for a chr1 grid (mapping scope = genome-wide).")
  write_tsv(hcp_opt, file.path(params$table_dir, "hcp_optimization.tsv"))
  write_tsv(k_star, file.path(params$table_dir, "hcp_kstar.tsv"))
} else {
  cat("Per-modality HCP optimization output not found in the archive — section skipped.\n")
}
```

`r if (exists("hcp_opt") && nrow(hcp_opt) > 0) sprintf("Module 25b estimates HCPs from each modality's own harmonized matrix at candidate k = 0–100 (step 5) on the pruned fixed covariate set (no cap), maps a chr1 phenotype subset per k, and selects k* by eGene yield with ties to the smaller k; every ancestry × modality run then mapped with its own matched covariate set. Chosen k* span %d–%d across the %d ancestry × modality cells (table above). The spread is the scientifically important result: EUR splicing and intron retention optimize at k = %d, far below the EUR expression optimum (k = %d), and the EUR splicing layer — which carried no detectable signal under expression-derived covariates — yields %d FDR ≤ 5%% eGenes with splicing-matched factors (Landscape). EAS splicing is the counterpoint: eGene yield is flat across its entire grid (≤ %d chr1 eGenes at every k), so its near-null result is robust to HCP specification rather than a consequence of it.", min(k_star$k), max(k_star$k), nrow(k_star), k_star$k[k_star$ancestry == "EUR" & k_star$modality == "splicing"], k_star$k[k_star$ancestry == "EUR" & k_star$modality == "expression"], n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EUR" & n_eg_mod$modality == "splicing"], max(hcp_opt$n_egenes[hcp_opt$ancestry == "EAS" & hcp_opt$modality == "splicing"]))`

## Permutation-calibrated p-value QQ plots

```{r fig-qq, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
qq <- bind_rows(
  combined %>% select(ancestry, modality, pval_beta),
  grouped %>% select(ancestry, modality, pval_beta)
) %>% group_by(ancestry, modality) %>%
  group_modify(~ qq_data(.x$pval_beta)) %>% ungroup()
# thin the null bulk for plotting; keep the full tail (observed > 3)
qq_plot <- qq %>% group_by(ancestry, modality) %>%
  filter(observed >= 3 | dplyr::row_number() %% 25 == 0) %>% ungroup()

p5 <- ggplot(qq_plot, aes(expected, observed, color = modality)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(MODALITY_COLORS, combined = "#D62728"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "expected -log10(pval_beta)", y = "observed -log10(pval_beta)") +
  theme_report()
print(p5)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_qq_pval_beta.png"), p5,
       width = 10, height = 5.2, dpi = 150)
```

```{r qq-stats}
lambda_tab <- bind_rows(grouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(ancestry, modality) %>%
  summarise(lambda = median(qchisq(1 - pval_beta, 1), na.rm = TRUE) /
              qchisq(0.5, 1), .groups = "drop")
lambda_eas_spl <- lambda_tab$lambda[lambda_tab$ancestry == "EAS" &
                                    lambda_tab$modality == "splicing"]
lambda_eur_spl <- lambda_tab$lambda[lambda_tab$ancestry == "EUR" &
                                    lambda_tab$modality == "splicing"]
lambda_signal <- range((lambda_tab %>%
                        filter(!(ancestry == "EAS" & modality == "splicing")))$lambda)
```

Two reference points calibrate the reading. **EAS splicing — the
lowest-signal layer (a handful of FDR ≤ 5% hits) — departs from the
diagonal only mildly** (genomic-control λ at the median =
`r round(lambda_eas_spl, 2)`), while every signal-bearing layer, EUR
splicing now included (λ = `r round(lambda_eur_spl, 2)`), departs upward
broadly and early with λ at the median of
`r round(lambda_signal[1], 2)`–`r round(lambda_signal[2], 2)` — the
expected QQ signature when a substantial fraction of tests are true
associations (Storey π1 up to
`r round(100 * max(pi1_cells$pi1, na.rm = TRUE))`%; below). The EAS
splicing curve is the calibration control: technical inflation from the
shared mapping machinery would bend it like the signal-bearing layers, and
it is instead the flattest curve on the plot — the calibration is honest
where signal is weakest, and the EUR splicing departure matches the
signature of its FDR-significant catalog rather than of artifact.

## Signal fraction (Storey π1) per layer

```{r pi1-table}
pi1_tab <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(layer, ancestry, modality) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pi1 = storey_pi1(pval_beta), min_q = min(qval),
            .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(layer, ancestry, desc(pi1))
knitr::kable(pi1_tab, digits = 3,
             caption = "Storey pi1 (estimated fraction of true associations) on permutation-calibrated p-values.")
write_tsv(pi1_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "pi1_summary.tsv"))

# Compare the pipeline's Storey q-values with BH on pval_beta. With pi0 near
# 1 the two nearly coincide; as the signal fraction grows Storey is more
# liberal by up to the estimated pi0. Report max |q - BH| per ancestry
# (combined layer).
bh_check <- combined %>% group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(max_abs_q_minus_BH = max(abs(qval - p.adjust(pval_beta, method = "BH"))),
            .groups = "drop")
bh_eg <- combined %>% group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(storey = sum(qval <= 0.05),
            bh = sum(p.adjust(pval_beta, method = "BH") <= 0.05),
            .groups = "drop") %>% tibble::column_to_rownames("ancestry")
```

```{r pi1-text}
pi1_range <- range(pi1_tab$pi1, na.rm = TRUE)
```

π1 estimates are `r round(100*pi1_range[1])`–`r round(100*pi1_range[2])`%
across all cells`r if (pi1_range[2] <= 0.05) " — at most a trace signal fraction, concentrated in the highest-signal layers" else sprintf(", with the largest fractions in %s", paste(pi1_tab %>% slice_max(pi1, n = 2) %>% mutate(lbl = paste(ancestry, modality, layer)) %>% pull(lbl), collapse = " and "))`.
`r if (max(bh_check$max_abs_q_minus_BH) < 0.05) sprintf("Storey q-values remain close to BH on this data (max |q − BH| across the combined layer = %s), as expected at low signal fractions.", signif(max(bh_check$max_abs_q_minus_BH), 2)) else sprintf("Storey q-values diverge from BH exactly where they should: in high-π1 cells the estimated π0 < 1 deflates q-values relative to BH (max |q − BH| across the combined layer = %s, at the null end of the ranked list where BH q-values approach 1). At the FDR ≤ 5%% boundary the π0 lift admits %d vs %d (EAS) and %d vs %d (EUR) combined-layer eGenes for Storey vs BH — the expected, conservative behavior.", signif(max(bh_check$max_abs_q_minus_BH), 2), bh_eg["EAS", "storey"], bh_eg["EAS", "bh"], bh_eg["EUR", "storey"], bh_eg["EUR", "bh"])`

## Power analysis

```{r power-curve, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ns <- seq(50, 500, by = 5)
alpha_expr <- 0.05 / (grouped %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS",
                                         modality == "expression") %>% nrow())
pow_curve <- tibble(n = ns,
                    r2 = sapply(ns, min_detectable_r2, alpha = alpha_expr, power = 0.8))
p6 <- ggplot(pow_curve, aes(n, r2)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(n_samp["EAS"], n_samp["EUR"], 445),
             linetype = c(2, 2, 3), color = c("#0279EE", "#FF9400", "grey40")) +
  annotate("text", x = n_samp["EAS"], y = 0.87, hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("EAS (n≈%d)", n_samp["EAS"])) +
  annotate("text", x = n_samp["EUR"], y = 0.80, hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("EUR (n≈%d)", n_samp["EUR"])) +
  annotate("text", x = 445, y = 0.73, label = "PANTRY/Geuvadis (n=445)", hjust = 1.05, size = 3.5) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 50, xmax = 500, ymin = 0.05, ymax = 0.15,
           alpha = 0.15, fill = "#75A025") +
  annotate("text", x = 490, y = 0.10, label = "typical cis-xQTL effect range", hjust = 1, size = 3.5) +
  labs(x = "sample size", y = "minimum detectable r² (80% power)") +
  theme_report()
print(p6)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_power_curve.png"), p6,
       width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r power-table}
power_tab <- bind_rows(
  grouped %>% group_by(ancestry, modality) %>% summarise(n_tested = n(), .groups = "drop"),
  combined %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% summarise(modality = "combined", n_tested = n(), .groups = "drop")
) %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(alpha = 0.05 / n_tested,
         n = n_samp[as.character(ancestry)],
         min_r2_our_n = min_detectable_r2(n, alpha),
         min_r2_pantry_n = min_detectable_r2(445, alpha)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% select(-n)
knitr::kable(power_tab, digits = 3,
             caption = "Minimum detectable effect (r², 80% power) at our sample sizes vs PANTRY's n=445, per layer.")
write_tsv(power_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "power_analysis.tsv"))
```

At n ≈ `r n_samp["EUR"]` (EUR), only xQTLs explaining ≳ 19% of phenotype
variance are detectable at genome-wide thresholds; the larger EAS stratum
(n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`) brings the floor to ≈ 10% — versus ≈ 6% at PANTRY's
n = 445. For reference, PANTRY (n = 445) reported 6,798 eGenes and a 66%
discovery gain from non-expression modalities; GTEx tissues at n ≈ 150
typically report hundreds to ~2,000 eGenes. The yield
(`r sum(n_xp)` FDR ≤ 5% phenotype-level associations; `r sum(n_eg)`
combined-layer eGenes) sits
`r if (sum(n_eg) < 100) "at the pessimistic end of" else "within"` that
range.

## Carrier-count audit: MAC floor propagation

```{r carrier-check}
mac_tab <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(ancestry, layer) %>%
  summarise(min_carriers = min(ma_count), n_lt5 = sum(ma_count < 5),
            n_total = n(), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(mac_tab,
             caption = "Minimum minor-allele carrier counts per layer (mapping sample sets).")
write_tsv(mac_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "carrier_count_audit.tsv"))
```

The MAC ≥ 5 floor is applied at the genotype intersection in module 23
(before outlier exclusion). `r if (all(mac_tab$n_lt5 == 0)) sprintf("The floor propagated cleanly: every tested pair in every layer retains ≥ %d minor-allele carriers in EAS and ≥ %d in EUR — no post-hoc carrier filtering is needed.", min(mac_tab$min_carriers[mac_tab$ancestry == "EAS"]), min(mac_tab$min_carriers[mac_tab$ancestry == "EUR"])) else "A fraction of tests retain < 5 carriers in the mapping sample sets (audit table) because the floor predates outlier exclusion and modality-specific sample attrition. No FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited; hit lists should be post-filtered to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source."`

# The landscape of placental xQTL regulation

*Modality-wise discovery landscape, following DevBrain Fig. 1. Two panels
that manuscript draws from external datasets are adapted or omitted:
eGene overlap and effect-size correlation against GTEx/PsychENCODE adult
brain (1B/1C) have no external placenta xQTL resource — GTEx lacks placenta
and the largest published placenta eQTL set (Peng 2017) is the RICHS
cohort, already inside this atlas — and are omitted; discovery context is
instead given against the published placenta eQTL literature (1A analog,
below). Inversion QTLs (1J) are not assayed by this pipeline.*

## Phenotypes and genes tested per modality

```{r test-counts}
counts <- bind_rows(
  grouped %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "genes_tested"),
  combined %>% count(ancestry, name = "genes_tested") %>% mutate(modality = "combined")
) %>% arrange(ancestry, modality)
knitr::kable(counts, caption = "Genes tested per ancestry × modality (grouped layers).")
write_tsv(counts, file.path(params$table_dir, "test_counts.tsv"))
```

```{r fig-phenotypes-genes, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
pheno_counts <- ungrouped %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "n_phenotypes")
expr_counts <- grouped %>% filter(modality == "expression") %>%
  count(ancestry, modality, name = "n_phenotypes")
pheno_counts <- bind_rows(pheno_counts, expr_counts)
gene_counts <- grouped %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "n_genes")

p1a <- ggplot(pheno_counts, aes(modality, n_phenotypes, fill = modality)) +
  geom_col() + facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "phenotypes tested") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
p1b <- ggplot(gene_counts, aes(modality, n_genes, fill = modality)) +
  geom_col() + facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "genes tested") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
p1 <- p1a + p1b + patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
print(p1)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig1_phenotypes_genes_per_modality.png"), p1,
       width = 10, height = 4.6, dpi = 150)
```

Note the ancestry asymmetry: EUR contributes roughly 1.5–5.6× more phenotypes
than EAS in the ungrouped layer (ancestry-specific phenotype filtering;
1.5× for splicing up to 5.6× for RNA editing),
while the gene universes are similar (~12–13k genes). Mapping sample sizes
vary slightly by modality (EAS `r n_range["EAS"]`, EUR `r n_range["EUR"]`
across layers, inferred from allele-count/frequency denominators) because
each modality's phenotype matrix harmonizes to a slightly different sample
set.

## Discovery in the context of published placenta eQTL studies

*DevBrain Fig. 1A analog: eGene discovery versus sample size. Published
values are hardcoded from the papers (captions/abstracts); note that Peng
2017 (RICHS) and Choi 2024 (SNUH) cohorts contribute to this atlas, so
their points mark the ancestry-stratified predecessors of the present
analysis rather than independent references.*

```{r fig-literature-discovery, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.5}
lit <- tribble(

  "This study (EAS)", n_samp[["EAS"]], n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EAS" & n_eg_mod$modality == "expression"], "This study (EAS)"
) %>% mutate(this_study = grepl("This study", study))
p_lit <- ggplot(lit, aes(n, egenes)) +
```
