
This study's per-stratum expression-layer eGene counts
(`r fmt(n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EAS" & n_eg_mod$modality == "expression"])`
EAS at n = `r n_samp[["EAS"]]`;
`r fmt(n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EUR" & n_eg_mod$modality == "expression"])`
EUR at n = `r n_samp[["EUR"]]`) sit on the literature
discovery-versus-size trend; the atlas additionally contributes the eight
non-expression modalities that none of the published studies assay.

## xQTL associations per modality — q-value tiers

*Discovery panel on the ungrouped (phenotype-level) layer — the fine-mapping
input set — with expression contributed by its per-gene primary scan.
DevBrain reports the analogous discovery counts per modality at FDR ≤ 5%.*

At FDR ≤ 5% the phenotype-level discovery layer contains
**`r sum(n_xp)` associations** (`r n_xp["EAS"]` EAS, `r n_xp["EUR"]` EUR)
across `r n_xp_genes["EAS"]` / `r n_xp_genes["EUR"]` unique genes; the
combined cross-modality layer adds `r sum(n_eg)` gene-level eGenes. The
figure shows the full q-value landscape: phenotypes binned by q-value per
ancestry × modality. Splicing splits by ancestry: EUR splicing reaches the
q ≤ 0.05 tier, while EAS splicing remains near-null — best q-value
`r signif(min((ungrouped %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS", modality == "splicing"))$qval), 2)`
— so the EAS splicing bar sits almost entirely in the q > 0.50 tier.

```{r fig-xgenes-tiers, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
tiers <- xpheno %>%
  select(ancestry, modality, phenotype_id, qval) %>%
  mutate(modality = factor(modality, levels = MODALITY_LEVELS),
         tier = cut(qval, breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 1),
                    labels = c("q≤0.05", "q≤0.10", "q≤0.25", "q≤0.50", "q>0.50"),
                    include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  count(ancestry, modality, tier, .drop = FALSE)
tier_cols <- c("q≤0.05" = "#D62728", "q≤0.10" = "#FF9400", "q≤0.25" = "#E9ED4C",
               "q≤0.50" = "#9ECAE1", "q>0.50" = "grey85")
p2 <- ggplot(tiers, aes(modality, n, fill = factor(tier, levels = names(tier_cols)))) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tier_cols, name = "q-value\nper phenotype") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "phenotypes") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
print(p2)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig2a_xphenotypes_qvalue_tiers.png"), p2,
       width = 10, height = 5.2, dpi = 150)
```

## Conditionally independent signals per gene

*DevBrain Fig. 1H analog: the distribution of conditionally independent
signals per tested unit, from the stepwise (`cis.map_independent`) scans —
now run on the grouped, ungrouped, and combined layers alike.*

```{r stepwise-stats}
# conditionally independent signals per unit (rank 1 = primary lead);
# unit = gene group (grouped/combined) or phenotype (ungrouped)
indep_summary <- if (nrow(independent) > 0 && "rank" %in% names(independent)) {
  independent %>%
    group_by(layer, ancestry, modality, phenotype_id) %>%
    summarise(n_signals = max(rank), .groups = "drop")
} else {
  tibble(layer = character(), ancestry = character(), modality = character(),
         phenotype_id = character(), n_signals = integer())
}
n_units_stepwise <- nrow(indep_summary)
n_secondary <- sum(indep_summary$n_signals > 1)
```

`r if (n_units_stepwise == 0) "No unit entered the stepwise scan (no FDR ≤ 5% entrant in any ancestry × modality layer), so no conditionally independent signals were called." else sprintf("Stepwise regression (cis.map_independent) ran on %s FDR-qualifying units across the three layers; %s (%.1f%%) carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (rank ≥ 2).", format(n_units_stepwise, big.mark = ','), format(n_secondary, big.mark = ','), 100 * n_secondary / n_units_stepwise)`

```{r fig-independent-signals, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
sig_dist <- indep_summary %>%
  mutate(n_signals_c = pmin(n_signals, 4L),
         layer = factor(layer, levels = c("grouped", "ungrouped", "combined"))) %>%
  count(layer, ancestry, n_signals_c)
p_ind <- ggplot(sig_dist, aes(factor(n_signals_c), n, fill = ancestry)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.72) +
  facet_wrap(~layer, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(EAS = "#0072B2", EUR = "#D55E00")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "conditionally independent signals per unit (4 = ≥4)",
       y = "units", fill = NULL) +
  theme_report() + theme(legend.position = "top")
print(p_ind)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_independent_signals.png"), p_ind,
       width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
```

Units are gene groups in the grouped/combined layers and individual
phenotypes in the ungrouped layer; only FDR ≤ 5% entrants undergo the
stepwise scan. The design-level view below shows how many phenotypes each
gene contributes to its group (the multiple-testing unit).

```{r fig-tss-by-rank, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5, eval=n_secondary > 0}
# DevBrain fig. S3M/N analog: primary signals sit closer to the TSS than
# secondary+ signals (allelic heterogeneity is more distal)
rank_dist <- independent %>%
  filter(!is.na(rank), !is.na(start_distance)) %>%
  mutate(rank_c = factor(pmin(rank, 4L), levels = 1:4,
                         labels = c("1st", "2nd", "3rd", "4th+")),
         abs_kb = abs(start_distance) / 1000)
wil <- tryCatch(
  wilcox.test(abs_kb ~ (rank_c == "1st"), data = rank_dist),
  error = function(e) NULL)
p_rank <- ggplot(rank_dist, aes(rank_c, abs_kb, fill = ancestry)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, outlier.alpha = 0.4, width = 0.6,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(EAS = "#0072B2", EUR = "#D55E00"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "conditional rank", y = "|distance to phenotype start| (kb)") +
  theme_report()
print(p_rank)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_tss_distance_by_rank.png"), p_rank,
       width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
```

`r if (n_secondary > 0 && exists("wil") && !is.null(wil)) sprintf("Primary (rank-1) signals are closer to the phenotype start than secondary signals (median %.2f vs %.2f kb; Wilcoxon p = %s) — the allelic-heterogeneity pattern DevBrain reports (their fig. S3M/N).", median(rank_dist$abs_kb[rank_dist$rank_c == "1st"]), median(rank_dist$abs_kb[rank_dist$rank_c != "1st"]), signif(wil$p.value, 2)) else ""`

```{r fig-group-size, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
gs <- bind_rows(
  grouped %>% filter(modality != "expression") %>%
    select(ancestry, modality, group_size),
  combined %>% select(ancestry, modality, group_size)
)
p3 <- ggplot(gs, aes(modality, group_size, fill = modality)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(MODALITY_COLORS, combined = "#ECE9E2"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "phenotypes per gene group (log10)") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
print(p3)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig2b_phenotypes_per_group.png"), p3,
       width = 10, height = 4.4, dpi = 150)
```

Combined groups integrate a median of ~4–5 phenotypes per gene (max > 100) —
the cross-modality burden-sharing the PANTRY design exploits. (Stability
shows a flat box at 1 by design: one phenotype per gene.)

## Lead-variant distance from the TSS

*DevBrain Fig. 1E analog: signed distance of each lead variant from its
target's start versus association strength, every tested gene shown —
significant xQTLs cluster sharply at the TSS.*

```{r fig-variant-position, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
tss_pts <- grouped %>%
  mutate(tss_kb = start_distance / 1000,
         modality = factor(modality, levels = MODALITY_LEVELS)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(qval), qval > 0)
# thin the non-significant bulk for plotting; keep all FDR <= 5% points
tss_plot <- bind_rows(
  tss_pts %>% filter(qval <= 0.05),
  tss_pts %>% filter(qval > 0.05) %>%
    group_by(ancestry, modality) %>%
    slice_sample(n = 1500) %>% ungroup())
p4 <- ggplot(tss_plot, aes(tss_kb, -log10(qval), color = modality)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 3, color = "grey50",
             linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 0.35, alpha = 0.45, stroke = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey40",
             linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_color_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, name = NULL,
                     guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2.5,
                                                              alpha = 1))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1000, 1000)) +
  labs(x = "distance of lead variant from phenotype start (kb)",
       y = expression(-log[10](q))) +
  theme_report() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(p4)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig2d_tss_distance_scatter.png"), p4,
       width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
```

Every tested gene's lead variant (grouped layers; non-significant bulk
thinned to 1,500 points per modality for plotting). The vertical
enrichment of points above the FDR ≤ 5% line near 0 kb is the expected
TSS-proximal concentration of causal cis-regulatory variants.

## Cross-modality overlap of xGenes

*DevBrain Fig. 1D analog: overlap among the modality-specific gene-level
catalogs (grouped layers, FDR ≤ 5%), per ancestry.*

```{r egene-overlap, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
# modality overlap of grouped eGenes, per ancestry (UpSet)
for (a in c("EAS", "EUR")) {
  sets <- split(egenes_grouped$gene_id[egenes_grouped$ancestry == a],
                egenes_grouped$modality[egenes_grouped$ancestry == a])
  sets <- sets[lengths(sets) > 0]
  if (length(sets) >= 2) {
    m <- ComplexHeatmap::make_comb_mat(sets)
    m <- m[ComplexHeatmap::comb_size(m) > 0]
    up <- ComplexHeatmap::UpSet(m, set_order = names(sets),
                                comb_order = order(-ComplexHeatmap::comb_size(m)))
    print(up)
    png(file.path(params$fig_dir, sprintf("fig_egene_upset_%s.png", tolower(a))),
        width = 9, height = 5, units = "in", res = 150)
    print(up)
    dev.off()
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("%s: %d modality set(s) with eGenes — UpSet needs ≥ 2; skipped.\n",
                a, length(sets)))
  }
}
```

## Functional annotation enrichment of lead variants

*DevBrain Fig. 1F analog: enrichment of fastVEP consequence classes and
regulatory-element overlaps (ENCODE cCRE classes, placenta OCRs) among
FDR ≤ 5% lead variants versus all tested lead variants — Fisher exact
log2 odds ratios per ancestry × modality. Rendered only when
lead_variant_annotations.tsv.gz is present in the archive (extraction
script 35, with the fastVEP two-pass).*

```{r fig-functional-enrichment, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, eval=!is.null(lead_annot)}
cons_classes <- c("splice_site", "coding_lof", "coding_nonsynonymous",
                  "synonymous", "utr", "intron", "regulatory_region",
                  "flanking", "intergenic", "other")
flag_cols <- setdiff(names(lead_annot),
                     c("variant_id", "chrom", "pos", "foreground_in",
                       "consequence"))
la <- lead_annot
for (cl in cons_classes)
  la[[paste0("cons_", cl)]] <- !is.na(la$consequence) & la$consequence == cl
for (cl in flag_cols)
  la[[cl]] <- tolower(as.character(la[[cl]])) %in% c("true", "1")
annot_cols <- c(paste0("cons_", cons_classes), flag_cols)
annot_labels <- c(setNames(paste0("VEP: ", cons_classes),
                           paste0("cons_", cons_classes)),
                  setNames(flag_cols, flag_cols))

fg <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped) %>%
  filter(qval <= fdr) %>% distinct(ancestry, modality, variant_id)
fg_cells <- fg %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "n_fg") %>%
  filter(n_fg >= 20)
fg_f <- fg %>% inner_join(fg_cells, by = c("ancestry", "modality"))

enrich <- fg_f %>%
  group_by(ancestry, modality) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    is_fg <- la$variant_id %in% .x$variant_id
    bind_rows(lapply(annot_cols, function(ac) {
      flag <- la[[ac]]
      a <- sum(is_fg & flag); b <- sum(is_fg & !flag)
      cc <- sum(!is_fg & flag); d <- sum(!is_fg & !flag)
      if (a < 3) return(NULL)
      if (min(a, b, cc, d) == 0) {
        a <- a + 0.5; b <- b + 0.5; cc <- cc + 0.5; d <- d + 0.5
      }
      or <- (a * d) / (b * cc)
      se <- sqrt(1 / a + 1 / b + 1 / cc + 1 / d)
      pv <- fisher.test(matrix(c(a, b, cc, d), nrow = 2))$p.value
      tibble(annotation = annot_labels[[ac]], log2or = log2(or),
             lo = log2(or) - 1.96 * se, hi = log2(or) + 1.96 * se,
             p = pv, n_fg_annot = a)
    }))
  }) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(modality = factor(modality, levels = MODALITY_LEVELS))

if (nrow(enrich) == 0) {
  cat("Annotation table present but no annotation class passed the minimum
      foreground counts — panel skipped.\n")
} else {
  annot_order <- enrich %>% group_by(annotation) %>%
    summarise(m = mean(log2or), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(m) %>% pull(annotation)
  enrich <- enrich %>% mutate(annotation = factor(annotation,
                                                  levels = annot_order))
  p_enr <- ggplot(enrich, aes(log2or, annotation, color = modality)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey60",
               linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
                   linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 1.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
    scale_color_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "log2 odds ratio (FDR ≤ 5% leads vs all tested leads)",
         y = NULL) +
    theme_report() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  print(p_enr)
  ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_functional_enrichment.png"), p_enr,
         width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)
  write_tsv(enrich, file.path(params$table_dir, "lead_variant_enrichment.tsv"))
}
```

`r if (is.null(lead_annot)) "*Skipped: lead_variant_annotations.tsv.gz is not in this archive — run 35_extract_report_extras.py (with the fastVEP two-pass) on seadragon and re-archive.*" else "Positive log2OR = over-representation among significant leads; bars are Wald 95% CIs on the log odds ratio (cells with fewer than 3 annotated foreground variants, or fewer than 20 foreground variants per ancestry × modality cell, are omitted; p-values unadjusted). The expected cis-regulatory signature is enrichment of regulatory-region/cCRE/OCR classes and depletion of intergenic sequence."`

## Cross-modality sharing of xQTL effects

*DevBrain Fig. 1H analog: Storey π1 replication rate of each modality's
FDR ≤ 5% lead (variant, gene) pairs against the nominal association of the
same variant across the gene's phenotypes in every other grouped modality,
per ancestry. Rendered only when cross_modality_lookup.tsv.gz is present.*

```{r fig-pi1-heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=5, eval=!is.null(xmod_lookup)}
pi1_mat <- xmod_lookup %>%
  group_by(ancestry, discovery_modality, replication_modality) %>%
  summarise(pi1 = storey_pi1(repl_pval),
            n = sum(!is.na(repl_pval)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(discovery_modality = factor(discovery_modality,
                                     levels = MODALITY_LEVELS),
         replication_modality = factor(replication_modality,
                                       levels = MODALITY_LEVELS)) %>%
  tidyr::complete(ancestry, discovery_modality, replication_modality)
p_pi1 <- ggplot(pi1_mat, aes(replication_modality, discovery_modality)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = pi1), color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(pi1) | n < 20, "",
                               sprintf("%.2f", pi1))), size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey88",
                       name = expression(pi[1])) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = MODALITY_LEVELS) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(MODALITY_LEVELS)) +
  labs(x = "replication modality", y = "discovery modality") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
print(p_pi1)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_cross_modality_pi1.png"), p_pi1,
       width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 150)
write_tsv(pi1_mat, file.path(params$table_dir, "cross_modality_pi1.tsv"))
```

`r if (is.null(xmod_lookup)) "*Skipped: cross_modality_lookup.tsv.gz is not in this archive — run 35_extract_report_extras.py on seadragon and re-archive.*" else "π1 = 1 − π0 (Storey, λ = 0.5) on replication-modality nominal p-values of each discovery modality's FDR ≤ 5% leads; the diagonal (self-replication) is not computed and cells with fewer than 20 tested pairs are left blank. High off-diagonal π1 indicates that one modality's regulatory variants recur as nominal associations in another — the cross-phenotype sharing the combined layer exploits."`

## Constraint of xGenes

*DevBrain Fig. 1G analog: gnomAD v2.1.1 loss-of-function constraint
(LOEUF) of combined-layer eGenes, split by driver modality, versus tested
non-eGenes. Rendered only when gene_constraint.tsv is present.*

```{r fig-constraint, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.8, eval=!is.null(constraint)}
eg_driver <- egenes_combined %>% distinct(ancestry, gene_id, driver_modality)
con_df <- combined %>%
  distinct(ancestry, gene_id) %>%
  left_join(eg_driver, by = c("ancestry", "gene_id")) %>%
  mutate(group = if_else(is.na(driver_modality), "non-eGene",
                         as.character(driver_modality)),
         group = factor(group, levels = c(MODALITY_LEVELS, "non-eGene"))) %>%
  left_join(constraint %>% select(gene_id, pLI, oe_lof), by = "gene_id")
con_loeuf <- con_df %>% filter(!is.na(oe_lof), !is.na(group))
wil_con <- lapply(c("EAS", "EUR"), function(a) {
  d <- con_loeuf %>% filter(ancestry == a)
  tryCatch(wilcox.test(oe_lof ~ (group == "non-eGene"), data = d),
           error = function(e) NULL)
}) %>% setNames(c("EAS", "EUR"))
p_con <- ggplot(con_loeuf, aes(group, oe_lof)) +
  geom_violin(aes(fill = group == "non-eGene"), scale = "width", trim = TRUE,
              color = NA, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.3,
               fill = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey70", `FALSE` = "#0279EE"),
                    guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "LOEUF (gnomAD oe/lof)") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
print(p_con)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_constraint_loeuf.png"), p_con,
       width = 10, height = 4.8, dpi = 150)
if (!is.null(wil_con$EAS) && !is.null(wil_con$EUR)) {
  med_con <- function(a, eg)
    median(con_loeuf$oe_lof[con_loeuf$ancestry == a &
                              (con_loeuf$group != "non-eGene") == eg])
  constraint_prose <- sprintf(
    paste0("Lower LOEUF = stronger constraint. eGenes are %s constrained ",
           "than tested non-eGenes (median LOEUF %.2f vs %.2f in EAS, ",
           "Wilcoxon p = %s; %.2f vs %.2f in EUR, p = %s) — the ",
           "dosage-sensitivity enrichment DevBrain reports for brain eGenes."),
    if (med_con("EAS", TRUE) < med_con("EAS", FALSE)) "more" else "less",
    med_con("EAS", TRUE), med_con("EAS", FALSE), signif(wil_con$EAS$p.value, 2),
    med_con("EUR", TRUE), med_con("EUR", FALSE), signif(wil_con$EUR$p.value, 2))
} else {
  constraint_prose <- paste0(
    "Lower LOEUF = stronger constraint; distributions shown per driver ",
    "modality versus tested non-eGenes (Wilcoxon test not computable).")
}
```

`r if (is.null(constraint)) "*Skipped: gene_constraint.tsv is not in this archive — run 35_extract_report_extras.py on seadragon and re-archive.*" else constraint_prose`

## Fine-mapped credible sets versus conditional signals

*DevBrain Fig. 1I analog: the number of SuSHiE credible sets per locus
versus the number of conditionally independent signals at the same
phenotype (maximum rank across ancestries in the stepwise scans). Rendered
only when the aggregated SuSHiE locus summary is present.*

```{r fig-cs-vs-conditional, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5.5, eval=!is.null(finemap_loci) && any(!is.na(finemap_loci$n_cs_out))}
cond_counts <- independent %>%
  filter(layer == "ungrouped" | (layer == "grouped" & modality == "expression")) %>%
  group_by(phenotype_id) %>%
  summarise(n_cond = max(rank), .groups = "drop")
cs_join <- finemap_loci %>%
  filter(!is.na(n_cs_out)) %>%
  inner_join(cond_counts, by = "phenotype_id")
cs_pts <- cs_join %>% count(n_cond, n_cs_out, name = "n_loci")
rho_cs <- if (nrow(cs_join) > 5)
  cor(cs_join$n_cond, cs_join$n_cs_out, method = "spearman") else NA_real_
p_cs <- ggplot(cs_pts, aes(n_cond, n_cs_out)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_loci), alpha = 0.55, color = "#0279EE") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 12, name = "loci") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(1)) +
  annotate("label", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.8,
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, label.size = 0, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("Spearman rho = %.2f\n(n = %s loci)", rho_cs,
                           fmt(nrow(cs_join)))) +
  labs(x = "conditionally independent signals (max across ancestries)",
       y = "SuSHiE credible sets per locus") +
  theme_report()
print(p_cs)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_cs_vs_conditional.png"), p_cs,
       width = 7.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
```

`r if (is.null(finemap_loci) || all(is.na(finemap_loci$n_cs_out))) "*Skipped: aggregated SuSHiE locus summary (finemap_locus_summary.tsv) is not in this archive — it is staged by make_report_archive.sh once 33_aggregate_finemap.py has run.*" else sprintf("%s of %s fine-mapped loci with credible sets matched a stepwise-conditional scan; the credible-set count tracks the conditional-signal count (Spearman rho = %.2f), cross-validating the two independence estimates.", fmt(nrow(cs_join)), fmt(sum(!is.na(finemap_loci$n_cs_out))), rho_cs)`

# Cross-ancestry regulation

*Following DevBrain Fig. 2: per-ancestry discovery (2B analog) and
cross-ancestry effect-size concordance (2C analog). When the enriched
archive is present (extraction script 35 + aggregated SuSHiE outputs), this
section additionally renders the lead-slope replication scatter (2C),
showcase-locus tracks (2E), and credible-set summaries (2D analog); without
it those panels skip with a note and the gene-level hexbin is the fallback
concordance view. Cross-ancestry analysis here is comparative only (no
pooled p-value combination).*

## Per-ancestry discovery comparison

```{r egene-ancestry-overlap}
# ancestry overlap of combined-layer eGenes
eg_eas <- unique(egenes_combined$gene_id[egenes_combined$ancestry == "EAS"])
eg_eur <- unique(egenes_combined$gene_id[egenes_combined$ancestry == "EUR"])
shared_eg <- intersect(eg_eas, eg_eur)
tested_both <- intersect(combined$gene_id[combined$ancestry == "EAS"],
                         combined$gene_id[combined$ancestry == "EUR"])
overlap_tab <- tibble(
  set = c("EAS only", "shared", "EUR only"),
  n = c(length(setdiff(eg_eas, eg_eur)), length(shared_eg),
        length(setdiff(eg_eur, eg_eas))))
# is the shared fraction more than chance given the two hit rates?
fisher_overlap <- if (length(tested_both) > 0 && (length(eg_eas) + length(eg_eur)) > 0) {
  fisher.test(matrix(c(length(shared_eg),
                       length(eg_eas) - length(shared_eg),
                       length(eg_eur) - length(shared_eg),
                       length(tested_both) - length(eg_eas) - length(eg_eur) + length(shared_eg)),
                     nrow = 2))[c("p.value", "estimate")]
} else NULL
knitr::kable(overlap_tab,
             caption = sprintf("Combined-layer eGene overlap between ancestries (genes tested in both: %s).",
                               format(length(tested_both), big.mark = ",")))
write_tsv(overlap_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "egene_ancestry_overlap.tsv"))
```

```{r fig-per-ancestry-discovery, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.8}
# (a) phenotype-level discoveries per modality by ancestry (ungrouped layer
#     + expression primary scan) — the fine-mapping input set
disc <- xpheno %>% filter(qval <= fdr) %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "n")
p_disc <- ggplot(disc, aes(modality, n, fill = ancestry)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(EAS = "#0072B2", EUR = "#D55E00")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "phenotype-level associations\n(FDR ≤ 5%)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
                         legend.position = "top")
# (b) combined-layer eGene overlap between ancestries
p_ov <- ggplot(overlap_tab, aes(set, n, fill = set)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(n)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("EAS only" = "#0072B2", "shared" = "#75A025",
                               "EUR only" = "#D55E00")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "combined-layer eGenes") +
  theme_report()
p_disc_wrap <- p_disc + p_ov + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(2.2, 1)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
print(p_disc_wrap)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_per_ancestry_discovery.png"), p_disc_wrap,
       width = 10, height = 4.8, dpi = 150)
```

`r if (!is.null(fisher_overlap)) sprintf("Of the %d EAS and %d EUR combined-layer eGenes, **%d are shared** (Fisher exact vs the tested-in-both universe: odds ratio %.2f, p = %s) — shared eGenes are %s than expected under independence.", length(eg_eas), length(eg_eur), length(shared_eg), fisher_overlap$estimate, signif(fisher_overlap$p.value, 2), if (fisher_overlap$estimate > 1) "more frequent" else "less frequent")`
The larger EUR discovery counts track its larger phenotype universe
(ancestry-specific filtering; Landscape) rather than a larger mapping
sample — EAS is the bigger stratum.

## Ancestry-specific versus shared eGenes

*DevBrain fig. S4 analog (adapted): composition of the EAS-only, shared,
and EUR-only combined-layer eGene sets — gene biotype (panel a) and, when
the constraint table is present, gnomAD LOEUF (panel b).*

```{r fig-ancestry-egene-sets, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.6}
eg_sets <- bind_rows(
  tibble(gene_id = setdiff(eg_eas, eg_eur), set = "EAS only"),
  tibble(gene_id = shared_eg, set = "shared"),
  tibble(gene_id = setdiff(eg_eur, eg_eas), set = "EUR only")) %>%
  mutate(set = factor(set, levels = c("EAS only", "shared", "EUR only")))
# (a) biotype composition
bt <- eg_sets %>%
  left_join(gene_map %>% select(gene_id, biotype), by = "gene_id") %>%
  mutate(biotype = ifelse(is.na(biotype) | biotype == "", "unknown", biotype))
top_bt <- bt %>% count(biotype, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_head(n = 6) %>%
  pull(biotype)
bt_levels <- c(setdiff(top_bt, c("other", "unknown")), "other", "unknown")
bt <- bt %>% mutate(biotype_c = factor(
  ifelse(biotype %in% top_bt, biotype, ifelse(biotype == "unknown", "unknown", "other")),
  levels = intersect(bt_levels, c(unique(biotype), "other", "unknown"))))
bt_pal <- setNames(c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#75A025", "#7B3294", "#FF9400",
                     "#0279EE", "#8C8C8C", "#ECE9E2")[seq_along(levels(bt$biotype_c))],
                   levels(bt$biotype_c))
p_bt <- ggplot(bt, aes(set, fill = biotype_c)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", width = 0.65) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = bt_pal, name = "biotype") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "fraction of eGenes") +
  theme_report()
# (b) LOEUF by set (needs the constraint table)
p_loeuf <- NULL
wil_sets <- NULL
if (!is.null(constraint)) {
  d_loeuf <- eg_sets %>%
    inner_join(constraint %>% select(gene_id, oe_lof), by = "gene_id") %>%
    filter(!is.na(oe_lof))
  wil_sets <- tryCatch(
    wilcox.test(oe_lof ~ (set == "shared"), data = d_loeuf),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  p_loeuf <- ggplot(d_loeuf, aes(set, oe_lof, fill = set)) +
    geom_violin(scale = "width", color = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.3,
                 fill = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("EAS only" = "#0072B2", "shared" = "#75A025",
                                 "EUR only" = "#D55E00"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "LOEUF (gnomAD oe/lof)") +
    theme_report()
}
p_sets <- if (is.null(p_loeuf)) p_bt else
  p_bt + p_loeuf + patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
print(p_sets)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_ancestry_egene_sets.png"), p_sets,
       width = if (is.null(p_loeuf)) 6 else 10, height = 4.6, dpi = 150)
if (!is.null(constraint) && !is.null(wil_sets)) {
  med_shared <- median(d_loeuf$oe_lof[d_loeuf$set == "shared"])
  med_spec <- median(d_loeuf$oe_lof[d_loeuf$set != "shared"])
  eg_sets_prose <- sprintf(
    paste0("Shared eGenes are %s constrained than ancestry-specific ones ",
           "(median LOEUF %.2f shared vs %.2f specific; Wilcoxon p = %s) — ",
           "genes with cross-ancestry regulatory signal trend toward dosage ",
           "sensitivity."),
    if (med_shared < med_spec) "more" else "less",
    med_shared, med_spec, signif(wil_sets$p.value, 2))
} else {
  eg_sets_prose <- "*LOEUF panel skipped: gene_constraint.tsv is not in this archive.*"
}
```

`r eg_sets_prose`

## Cross-ancestry effect-size concordance

*DevBrain Fig. 2C analog: consistency of xQTL effects between the two
ancestry strata. When the cross-ancestry lookup table is present this is
shown as the DevBrain discovery-vs-replication lead-slope scatter;
otherwise the gene-level −log10(p) hexbin below is the fallback view.*

```{r fig-concordance, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.5, eval=is.null(xanc_lookup)}
ea <- combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>% dedup_best() %>%
  select(gene_id, pval_beta_a = pval_beta)
eu <- combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EUR") %>% dedup_best() %>%
  select(gene_id, pval_beta_b = pval_beta)
jj <- ea %>% inner_join(eu, by = "gene_id")
rho <- cor(-log10(jj$pval_beta_a), -log10(jj$pval_beta_b), method = "spearman")

lim <- max(c(-log10(jj$pval_beta_a), -log10(jj$pval_beta_b))) * 1.05
p7 <- ggplot(jj, aes(-log10(pval_beta_a), -log10(pval_beta_b))) +
  geom_hex(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", name = "genes") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, lim), ylim = c(0, lim)) +
  annotate("label", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.8,
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, label.size = 0, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("Spearman rho = %.3f\n(n = %s genes tested in both)",
                           rho, format(nrow(jj), big.mark = ","))) +
  labs(x = "EAS  -log10(pval_beta), combined layer",
       y = "EUR  -log10(pval_beta), combined layer") +
  theme_report()
print(p7)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_cross_ancestry_concordance.png"), p7,
       width = 7.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r fig-cross-ancestry-slopes, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.4, eval=!is.null(xanc_lookup)}
# DevBrain Fig. 2C analog: discovery-ancestry lead slope vs the same
# (variant, phenotype) pair's slope in the other ancestry (targeted OLS
# lookup, extraction script 35). Discovery layer = ungrouped phenotypes +
# the expression primary scan (the fine-mapping input set).
xa <- xanc_lookup %>%
  filter(layer == "ungrouped" |
           (layer == "grouped" & modality == "expression")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(repl_slope), !is.na(discovery_slope), !is.na(repl_se)) %>%
  mutate(replicated = !is.na(repl_pval) & repl_pval < 0.05,
         panel = sprintf("%s-discovered, replicated in %s",
                         discovery_ancestry, replication_ancestry))
rho_xa <- xa %>% group_by(panel) %>%
  summarise(rho = cor(discovery_slope, repl_slope, method = "spearman"),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop")
p_xa <- ggplot(xa, aes(discovery_slope, repl_slope)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 3, color = "grey55") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey75",
             linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey75",
             linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = repl_slope - 1.96 * repl_se,
                    ymax = repl_slope + 1.96 * repl_se, color = replicated),
                width = 0, alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_point(aes(color = replicated), size = 1.0, alpha = 0.65, stroke = 0) +
  geom_smooth(aes(color = replicated), method = "lm", se = FALSE,
              linewidth = 0.7, formula = y ~ x) +
  geom_label(data = rho_xa,
             aes(label = sprintf("Spearman rho = %.2f\nn = %s", rho,
                                 fmt(n))),
             x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.1, size = 3.4,
             fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, label.size = 0, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#D55E00", `FALSE` = "grey65"),
                     name = "nominal replication\n(p < 0.05)") +
  labs(x = "discovery-ancestry slope (lead variant)",
       y = "replication-ancestry slope") +
  theme_report() + theme(legend.position = "top")
print(p_xa)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_cross_ancestry_slopes.png"), p_xa,
       width = 10, height = 5.4, dpi = 150)
xa_prose <- sprintf(
  paste0("Each point is an FDR ≤ 5%% discovery-layer lead (variant, ",
         "phenotype) pair; the y-axis is the same pair's slope in the ",
         "other ancestry from a targeted lookup (bars: ±1.96·SE). Slopes ",
         "are on inverse-normal-transformed phenotypes — both strata ",
         "share the transform, so slopes (not aFC) are the comparable ",
         "effect scale here, a deliberate deviation from DevBrain's aFC ",
         "panel. Of %s looked-up pairs, %s (%.1f%%) replicate at nominal ",
         "p < 0.05 and direction agrees in %.1f%%."),
  fmt(nrow(xa)), fmt(sum(xa$replicated)), 100 * mean(xa$replicated),
  100 * mean(sign(xa$discovery_slope) == sign(xa$repl_slope)))
```

`r if (is.null(xanc_lookup)) "*Slope scatter skipped: cross_ancestry_lookup.tsv.gz is not in this archive — the hexbin above is the fallback view. Run 35_extract_report_extras.py on seadragon and re-archive.*" else xa_prose`

```{r concordance-tables}
conc_combined <- cross_ancestry_concordance(
  combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>% dedup_best(),
  combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EUR") %>% dedup_best()) %>%
  mutate(modality = "combined")
conc_mod <- grouped %>%
  group_by(modality) %>%
  group_modify(~ cross_ancestry_concordance(
    .x %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>% dedup_best(),
    .x %>% filter(ancestry == "EUR") %>% dedup_best())) %>% ungroup()
conc_all <- bind_rows(conc_mod, conc_combined) %>%
  select(modality, n_genes, same_variant, rank_spearman, top100_overlap)
knitr::kable(conc_all, digits = 3,
             caption = "Cross-ancestry concordance per layer: genes tested in both ancestries, same-lead-variant count, Spearman correlation of -log10(pval_beta), and top-100 gene overlap.")
write_tsv(conc_all, file.path(params$table_dir, "cross_ancestry_concordance.tsv"))
```

Rank concordance ranges from `r round(min(conc_all$rank_spearman, na.rm = TRUE), 3)` to
`r round(max(conc_all$rank_spearman, na.rm = TRUE), 3)` across layers
(top-100 overlap at or below chance).
`r if (max(abs(conc_all$rank_spearman), na.rm = TRUE) < 0.1) "The two ancestries' sub-threshold tails do **not** point at the same genes — consistent with sub-threshold ranks being dominated by noise rather than shared weak signal, and arguing against combining the strata for discovery at these sample sizes." else "Layers with non-trivial rank concordance indicate shared sub-threshold signal; see the table."`

## Showcase loci

*DevBrain Fig. 2E analog: regional association tracks for two showcase
loci — ERAP2 (the literature-recurrent placenta eQTL) and the top shared
non-expression-driver locus — per ancestry, points colored by LD (r²) to
the lead variant (diamond), gene models below. Rendered only when the
per-locus regional scans (locus_*.tsv.gz, extraction script 35) are in the
archive.*

```{r fig-locus-tracks, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, eval=!is.null(locus_scans)}
for (loc in unique(locus_scans$locus)) {
  d <- locus_scans %>% filter(locus == loc)
  gid <- d$gene_id[1]
  lead <- d$lead_variant[1]
  mod <- d$modality[1]
  chrom <- sub("^chr", "", as.character(d$chrom[1]))
  win <- range(d$pos, na.rm = TRUE)
  tracks <- list()
  for (a in c("EAS", "EUR")) {
    da <- d %>% filter(ancestry == a)
    if (nrow(da) == 0) next
    tracks[[a]] <- ggplot(da, aes(pos / 1e6, -log10(repl_pval))) +
      geom_point(aes(color = r2_lead), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8, stroke = 0) +
      geom_point(data = da %>% filter(variant_id == lead),
                 shape = 23, fill = "#7B3294", color = "black", size = 2.6,
                 stroke = 0.4) +
      scale_color_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey70",
                            name = expression(r^2 ~ "to lead")) +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = win / 1e6) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = sprintf("%s -log10(p)", a)) +
      theme_report()
  }
  # gene-model track (skipped if gene_bodies is unavailable); novel-annotation
  # IDs without a symbol (HPLRG_*) are dropped from the track for readability
  p_gene <- NULL
  if (!is.null(gene_bodies)) {
    gb <- gene_bodies %>%
      mutate(chr_bare = sub("^chr", "", chr)) %>%
      filter(chr_bare == chrom, end >= win[1], start <= win[2]) %>%
      mutate(label = symd(gene_id)) %>%
      filter(gene_id == gid | label != gene_id) %>%
      arrange(desc(gene_id == gid), start) %>%
      mutate(lane = (row_number() - 1) %% 2)
    if (nrow(gb) > 0) {
      if (nrow(gb) > 24) gb$label[gb$gene_id != gid & gb$lane == 1] <- ""
      p_gene <- ggplot(gb) +
        geom_rect(aes(xmin = pmax(start, win[1]) / 1e6,
                      xmax = pmin(end, win[2]) / 1e6,
                      ymin = lane - 0.28, ymax = lane + 0.28,
                      fill = gene_id == gid), color = NA) +
        geom_text(aes(x = (pmax(start, win[1]) + pmin(end, win[2])) / 2e6,
                      y = lane + 0.42, label = label,
                      fontface = ifelse(gene_id == gid, "bold", "plain")),
                  size = 2.3, vjust = 0, check_overlap = TRUE) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#D55E00", `FALSE` = "grey70"),
                          guide = "none") +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = win / 1e6, ylim = c(-0.5, 2.1)) +
        labs(x = sprintf("chr%s position (Mb)", chrom), y = NULL) +
        theme_report() +
        theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
    }
  }
  panels <- c(tracks, list(p_gene))
  panels <- panels[!sapply(panels, is.null)]
  p_loc <- patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 1, guides = "collect",
                                 heights = c(rep(2, length(tracks)),
                                             if (is.null(p_gene)) NULL else 1.2)) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(title = sprintf("%s locus (%s)", symd(gid), mod))
  print(p_loc)
  ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, sprintf("fig_locus_%s.png", loc)), p_loc,
         width = 9, height = 2.2 * length(panels) + 1, dpi = 150)
}
```

`r if (is.null(locus_scans)) "*Skipped: no locus_*.tsv.gz regional scans in this archive — run 35_extract_report_extras.py on seadragon (default loci: ERAP2 plus the top shared non-expression-driver locus) and re-archive.*" else "The lead variant (purple diamond) sits in a TSS-proximal LD block; ancestry differences in the tracks reflect both LD structure and true effect heterogeneity, which the joint SuSHiE fine-mapping quantifies formally."`

## SuSHiE credible-set summary

*DevBrain Fig. 2D analog (conditional): size distribution of purity-pruned
credible sets and the cross-ancestry effect-correlation estimates, from the
aggregated SuSHiE outputs. Rendered only when
finemap_credible_sets.tsv.gz is present; per-locus detail remains in
report_finemap.*

```{r fig-cs-sizes, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.4, eval=!is.null(finemap_cs)}
cs <- finemap_cs
p_size <- ggplot(cs, aes(n_variants)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#0279EE", color = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "credible-set size (variants, log10)", y = "credible sets") +
  theme_report()
corr_cols <- grep("_est_corr$", names(cs), value = TRUE)
p_corr <- NULL
if (length(corr_cols) > 0) {
  cd <- cs %>% select(all_of(corr_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "pair", values_to = "corr",
                 values_drop_na = TRUE)
  p_corr <- ggplot(cd, aes(corr)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#75A025", color = "white",
                   linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 3, color = "grey50",
               linewidth = 0.4) +
    labs(x = "SuSHiE cross-ancestry effect correlation", y = "credible sets") +
    theme_report()
}
p_fm <- if (is.null(p_corr)) p_size else
  p_size + p_corr + patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
print(p_fm)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_finemap_cs_summary.png"), p_fm,
       width = if (is.null(p_corr)) 6 else 10, height = 4.4, dpi = 150)
cs_prose <- sprintf(
  paste0("Median credible-set size is %s variants (n = %s credible sets ",
         "across %s loci)%s."),
  fmt(median(finemap_cs$n_variants, na.rm = TRUE)), fmt(nrow(finemap_cs)),
  fmt(length(unique(finemap_cs$phenotype_id))),
  if (length(corr_cols) > 0)
    sprintf(paste0("; the cross-ancestry effect-correlation distribution ",
                   "centers at %.2f, quantifying how shared the causal ",
                   "effects are between strata"),
            median(unlist(finemap_cs[, corr_cols]), na.rm = TRUE)) else "")
```

`r if (is.null(finemap_cs)) "*Skipped: finemap_credible_sets.tsv.gz is not in this archive — it is staged by make_report_archive.sh once 33_aggregate_finemap.py has run.*" else cs_prose`

# Discovery catalog

## FDR-significant associations

```{r hit-table}
hit_tab <- hits %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = symd(gene_id),
         modality_display = if_else(layer == "combined",
                                    paste0("combined (driver: ", driver_modality, ")"),
                                    as.character(modality)),
         target = str_split_fixed(original_id, "__", 2)[, 2],
         # distance to the target itself: parse the coordinate when the
         # phenotype id encodes one (e.g. RNA-editing sites); otherwise use
         # tensorQTL's start_distance (distance to the phenotype TSS)
         target_pos = suppressWarnings(
           as.numeric(str_match(target, "^chr[0-9XYM]+_(\\d+)$")[, 2])),
         variant_to_target_kb = round(abs(if_else(!is.na(target_pos),
                                                  variant_pos - target_pos,
                                                  start_distance)) / 1000)) %>%
  arrange(ancestry, layer, qval) %>%
  select(ancestry, layer, modality_display, gene_id, gene_symbol, phenotype_id,
         target, variant_id, af, ma_count, slope, pval_nominal, pval_beta,
         qval, variant_to_target_kb)
knitr::kable(hit_tab %>% slice_head(n = 100), digits = 3,
             caption = sprintf("FDR ≤ 5%% associations across layers (top 100 of %s shown; full table in tables/fdr_hits.tsv). Grouped/combined rows are gene-level; ungrouped rows are phenotype-level.", format(nrow(hit_tab), big.mark = ",")))
write_tsv(hit_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "fdr_hits.tsv"))
```

Per-gene context tables show each FDR-significant gene across all layers and
both ancestries (grouped/combined rows are gene-level; ungrouped rows are
phenotype-level leads). Read the pattern per gene: a hit confined to one
layer and one ancestry is ancestry- and modality-specific; a hit that also
passes in the combined layer survives the cross-modality grouping burden.

```{r hit-context, results='asis'}
hit_genes <- hits %>% distinct(ancestry, gene_id) %>% arrange(ancestry, gene_id)
max_context <- 12
ctx_genes <- hit_genes %>% slice_head(n = max_context)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ctx_genes))) {
  g <- ctx_genes$gene_id[i]
  a <- as.character(ctx_genes$ancestry[i])
  ctx <- bind_rows(
    grouped %>% filter(gene_id == g) %>%
      select(ancestry, modality, layer, variant_id, af, ma_count, pval_beta, qval),
    combined %>% filter(gene_id == g) %>%
      select(ancestry, modality = driver_modality, layer, variant_id, af,
             ma_count, pval_beta, qval),
    ungrouped %>% filter(gene_id == g) %>%
      select(ancestry, modality, layer, variant_id, af, ma_count, pval_beta, qval)
  ) %>% arrange(ancestry, qval)
  cat(sprintf("\n\n#### %s — %s\n\n", a, symd(g)))
  print(knitr::kable(ctx, digits = 3,
                     caption = sprintf("%s (%s) across layers and ancestries.",
                                       symd(g), g)))
}
if (nrow(hit_genes) > max_context) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n*%s further hit genes omitted from per-gene context tables; see tables/fdr_hits.tsv.*\n",
              format(nrow(hit_genes) - max_context, big.mark = ",")))
}
```

All hits clear the MAC ≥ 5 carrier floor (audit in Calibration); visual QC
of phenotype levels by genotype and replication in larger placental cohorts
remain the required next steps before functional claims.

## Conditionally independent secondary signals

`r if (n_units_stepwise == 0) "No unit reached FDR ≤ 5% in any ancestry × modality layer, so no cell produced a stepwise entrant and all independent-signal outputs are empty by design." else sprintf("Of the %s FDR-qualifying units entering the stepwise scan, **%s carry a conditionally independent secondary signal** (rank ≥ 2); the remainder yielded their primary lead variant alone.", format(n_units_stepwise, big.mark = ','), format(n_secondary, big.mark = ','))`

```{r stepwise-table}
if (n_secondary > 0) {
  # group_id exists for grouped/combined runs, absent for expression and
  # ungrouped runs; fall back to parsing the phenotype id
  gid <- if ("group_id" %in% names(independent)) {
    strip_version(if_else(is.na(independent$group_id),
                          str_split_fixed(independent$phenotype_id, "__", 2)[, 1],
                          independent$group_id))
  } else {
    strip_version(str_split_fixed(independent$phenotype_id, "__", 2)[, 1])
  }
  sec <- independent %>%
    mutate(gene_id = gid, gene_symbol = symd(gene_id)) %>%
    filter(rank >= 2) %>%
    select(ancestry, layer, modality, gene_id, gene_symbol, phenotype_id,
           variant_id, rank, slope, pval_nominal, pval_beta)
  knitr::kable(sec %>% slice_head(n = 100), digits = 3,
               caption = sprintf("Conditionally independent secondary signals (rank ≥ 2; top 100 of %s shown; full table in tables/independent_secondary.tsv).", format(nrow(sec), big.mark = ",")))
  write_tsv(sec, file.path(params$table_dir, "independent_secondary.tsv"))
}
```

```{r egene-catalog}
catalog_xpheno <- xpheno_hits %>%
```

The gene-level catalog is the **combined cross-modality layer**
(`r n_eg["EAS"]` EAS / `r n_eg["EUR"]` EUR eGenes; full table in
`tables/egene_catalog_combined.tsv`); the per-modality grouped breakdown is
in `tables/egene_catalog_by_modality.tsv`, and the phenotype-level discovery
set (ungrouped + expression; the SuSHiE fine-mapping input) is in
`tables/xqtl_catalog_phenotype_level.tsv`. The driver modality labels which
modality carries the gene's strongest association.

## Driver-modality resolution

The combined layer labels each gene-group by its **driver phenotype** (the
phenotype with the best nominal association in the group), and the ungrouped
layer provides per-phenotype lead variants. Applied to the FDR-significant
catalog, this resolves which modality and transcript carries each eGene
signal.

```{r fig-driver-modality, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
driver_tab <- combined %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>% mutate(rank_by_q = rank(qval, ties.method = "first")) %>%
  ungroup()
driver_comp <- bind_rows(
  driver_tab %>% filter(rank_by_q <= 50)  %>% count(ancestry, driver_modality) %>% mutate(tier = "top 50"),
  driver_tab %>% filter(rank_by_q <= 200) %>% count(ancestry, driver_modality) %>% mutate(tier = "top 200")
)
p8 <- ggplot(driver_comp, aes(driver_modality, n, fill = driver_modality)) +
  geom_col() + facet_grid(tier ~ ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "genes driven by modality") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
print(p8)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_driver_modality.png"), p8,
       width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
write_tsv(driver_comp, file.path(params$table_dir, "driver_modality_composition.tsv"))
```

```{r driver-shares}
shares <- driver_comp %>% filter(tier == "top 50") %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>% mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()
share_of <- function(anc, mod) {
  x <- shares %>% filter(ancestry == anc, driver_modality == mod)
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(0)
  round(100 * x$frac)
}
```

```{r driver-top}
top_driver <- shares %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% slice_max(frac, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

`r sprintf("%s drives the largest share of top-ranked genes in %s (%d%% of the top 50)", top_driver$driver_modality[top_driver$ancestry == "EAS"], "EAS", share_of("EAS", as.character(top_driver$driver_modality[top_driver$ancestry == "EAS"])))`;
`r sprintf("%s does so in %s (%d%% of the top 50)", top_driver$driver_modality[top_driver$ancestry == "EUR"], "EUR", share_of("EUR", as.character(top_driver$driver_modality[top_driver$ancestry == "EUR"])))`.

### Within-gene driver breakdown for the top combined genes

For the top 10 combined-layer genes per ancestry, the per-phenotype lead
associations across all modalities (ungrouped layer):

```{r driver-breakdown}
top10 <- top_combined %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  select(ancestry, gene_id, gene_symbol, driver_modality)
breakdown <- top10 %>%
  inner_join(ungrouped %>% select(ancestry, gene_id, modality, phenotype_id,
                                  variant_id, af, slope, pval_beta, qval),
             by = c("ancestry", "gene_id")) %>%
  group_by(ancestry, gene_id) %>% arrange(pval_beta, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = symd(gene_id)) %>%
  select(ancestry, gene_id, gene_symbol, modality, phenotype_id, variant_id,
         af, slope, pval_beta, qval)
write_tsv(breakdown, file.path(params$table_dir, "driver_breakdown_top10.tsv"))
knitr::kable(breakdown %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>%
               select(-ancestry) %>% head(20), digits = 3,
             caption = "EAS top-10 genes: top 5 phenotypes each (ungrouped layer).")
```

# Functional characterization

*eGene-set functional enrichment, in the style of DevBrain Fig. S4D.*

## Functional enrichment (g:Profiler)

```{r enrichment, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
# Over-representation analysis on the combined-layer eGene sets, g:Profiler
# gost with g:SCS correction; background = all genes tested in the
# corresponding stratum (DevBrain custom-background convention).
enrich_results <- list()
if (requireNamespace("gprofiler2", quietly = TRUE) && nrow(egenes_combined) > 0) {
  bg_eas <- unique(combined$gene_id[combined$ancestry == "EAS"])
  bg_eur <- unique(combined$gene_id[combined$ancestry == "EUR"])
  enrich_sets <- list(
    "EAS combined eGenes"  = list(genes = eg_eas, bg = bg_eas),
    "EUR combined eGenes"  = list(genes = eg_eur, bg = bg_eur),
    "shared eGenes"        = list(genes = shared_eg, bg = tested_both),
    "EAS-specific eGenes"  = list(genes = setdiff(eg_eas, eg_eur), bg = bg_eas),
    "EUR-specific eGenes"  = list(genes = setdiff(eg_eur, eg_eas), bg = bg_eur)
  )
  for (nm in names(enrich_sets)) {
    es <- enrich_sets[[nm]]
    if (length(es$genes) < 5) {
      message(sprintf("  enrichment: '%s' has %d genes (< 5) — skipped", nm,
                      length(es$genes)))
      next
    }
    res <- tryCatch(
      gprofiler2::gost(es$genes, organism = "hsapiens", ordered_query = FALSE,
                       sources = c("GO:BP", "GO:MF", "GO:CC", "KEGG", "REAC"),
                       custom_bg = es$bg, correction_method = "g_SCS",
                       significant = TRUE),
      error = function(e) { message("  gost failed for '", nm, "': ", e$message); NULL })
    if (is.null(res) || is.null(res$result) || nrow(res$result) == 0) next
    enrich_results[[nm]] <- res$result %>%
      mutate(query_set = nm, n_query = length(es$genes)) %>%
      select(query_set, source, term_id, term_name, p_value, term_size,
             query_size, intersection_size, n_query, any_of("intersection"))
    write_tsv(enrich_results[[nm]],
              file.path(params$table_dir,
                        paste0("enrichment_", make.names(nm), ".tsv")))
  }
} else if (!requireNamespace("gprofiler2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("gprofiler2 not installed — enrichment skipped (install.packages('gprofiler2')).\n")
}

if (length(enrich_results) > 0) {
  enrich_all <- bind_rows(enrich_results)
  write_tsv(enrich_all, file.path(params$table_dir, "enrichment_all.tsv"))
  enrich_top <- enrich_all %>% group_by(query_set) %>%
    slice_min(p_value, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(term_label = str_wrap(term_name, 35),
           term_label = forcats::fct_reorder(term_label, -log10(p_value)))
  p_enrich <- ggplot(enrich_top,
                     aes(-log10(p_value), term_label, color = source,
                         size = intersection_size)) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~query_set, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = NULL) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "genes", range = c(1.5, 5)) +
    guides(size = guide_legend(title.position = "top"),
           color = guide_legend(title.position = "top")) +
    labs(x = "-log10(g:SCS-adjusted p)", y = NULL) +
    theme_report(base_size = 9) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  print(p_enrich)
  ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_enrichment_dotplot.png"), p_enrich,
         width = 9, height = max(4, 2.6 * length(enrich_results)), dpi = 150)
  knitr::kable(enrich_all %>% group_by(query_set) %>%
                 slice_min(p_value, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
                 select(query_set, source, term_id, term_name, p_value,
                        intersection_size),
               digits = 3,
               caption = "Top 5 enriched terms per eGene set (full tables in tables/enrichment_*.tsv).")
} else {
  cat("No enrichment results (all sets < 5 genes, no significant terms, or g:Profiler unreachable).\n")
}
```

Enrichment is over-representation analysis on the FDR ≤ 5% combined-layer
eGene sets (per ancestry, plus shared and ancestry-specific sets) against
the **tested-gene universe of the same stratum** — not the whole genome —
following the DevBrain xQTL convention; g:SCS is g:Profiler's native
multiple-testing correction. Sets with fewer than 5 genes are skipped (ORA
is not meaningful). Full term tables are in `tables/enrichment_*.tsv`.

# Biological interpretation

```{r interp-numbers}
mod_leader <- if (nrow(n_eg_mod) > 0) {
  n_eg_mod %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% mutate(total = sum(n)) %>%
    slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
} else NULL
enrich_highlight <- if (exists("enrich_results") && length(enrich_results) > 0) {
  bind_rows(enrich_results) %>% group_by(query_set) %>%
    slice_min(p_value, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
    summarise(hl = paste(sprintf("%s — %s (%s, g:SCS p = %s)", query_set,
                                 term_name, source, signif(p_value, 2)),
                         collapse = "; ")) %>% pull(hl)
} else NA_character_
```

**The discovery landscape: `r sum(n_xp)` FDR ≤ 5% phenotype-level
associations** (`r n_xp["EAS"]` EAS / `r n_xp["EUR"]` EUR, ungrouped +
expression layers) implicating `r n_xp_genes["EAS"]` / `r n_xp_genes["EUR"]`
unique genes, with the gene-level combined-layer catalog at
**`r n_eg["EAS"]` EAS and `r n_eg["EUR"]` EUR eGenes**
(n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`/`r n_samp["EUR"]`, MAF ≥
0.01 + MAC ≥ 5, genome-wide permutation calibration). Strongest per
ancestry:
`r paste(sprintf("%s: %s", top_by_anc$ancestry, apply(top_by_anc, 1, function(r) sprintf("%s (%s, %s layer, q = %s, r² ≈ %.2f)", symd(r[["gene_id"]]), r[["modality"]], r[["layer"]], signif(as.numeric(r[["qval"]]), 2), approx_r2(as.numeric(r[["slope"]]), as.numeric(r[["af"]]))))), collapse = "; ")`.
`r if (!is.null(hit_r2)) sprintf("Hit effect sizes (r² %.2f–%.2f) sit in the class the power floor permits.", hit_r2[1], hit_r2[2])`
All hits should be treated as candidates: visual QC of phenotype levels by
genotype and replication in larger placental cohorts come before functional
claims.

Three **characterization** observations:

1. **Modality composition.** `r if (!is.null(mod_leader)) paste(sprintf("%s leads the %s grouped-eGene breakdown (%d of %d)", mod_leader$modality, mod_leader$ancestry, mod_leader$n, mod_leader$total), collapse = "; ") else "No grouped-layer eGenes."`
   PANTRY's central finding was that non-expression modalities carry the
   largest share of regulatory signal; the driver-modality composition of
   the catalog (above) tests whether that ordering holds in placenta.
2. **Ancestry sharing.** `r if (!is.null(fisher_overlap)) sprintf("%d of %d EAS and %d EUR combined-layer eGenes are shared (Fisher OR %.2f, p = %s vs the tested-in-both universe).", length(shared_eg), length(eg_eas), length(eg_eur), fisher_overlap$estimate, signif(fisher_overlap$p.value, 2)) else "Ancestry overlap was not computed (empty eGene set)."`
   Shared eGenes are the cross-ancestry replication signal; specific sets
   are candidates for ancestry-biased regulation.
3. **Functional enrichment.** `r if (!is.na(enrich_highlight)) paste0("Top g:Profiler term per set: ", enrich_highlight, ". Full tables in tables/enrichment_*.tsv.") else "No significant enrichment terms (or sets too small for ORA) — see the enrichment section."`

## Literature context

**Positive control: the ERAP1/ERAP2 locus (5q15).** The strongest signal
shared across ancestries is *ERAP2* — a top-10 combined-layer gene in both
strata (EAS #6, q = 9.1×10⁻¹⁹, expression driver; EUR #3,
q = 1.3×10⁻²⁸, **isoform-expression** driver) — with *ERAP1* the #1 gene
in EUR (q = 2.0×10⁻³⁰, alt_polyA driver). *ERAP2* is a canonical preeclampsia risk
locus: fetal-genome variants at *ERAP2* associate with preeclampsia in
Australian/Norwegian ([Johnson et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00439-009-0714-x)),
Brazilian ([Ferreira et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-86240-z)),
and African American ([Hill et al. 2011](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2350-12-64))
cohorts, and ERAP1/ERAP2 are differentially expressed in preeclamptic
placentas ([Seamon et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2020.00396)).
The EUR driver being isoform expression is mechanism-consistent: the
preeclampsia-associated *ERAP2* variation tags a haplotype under balancing
selection whose molecular effect is alternative splicing and
nonsense-mediated decay of *ERAP2* transcripts
([Andrés et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1001157);
[Raja & Kuiper 2023](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41435-023-00225-8);
[Ye et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.240390.118)) — exactly the
phenotype class our isoform-expression layer measures. Recovering this
locus, through the expected modality, is direct evidence that the atlas
captures disease-relevant placental regulation.

**Top combined-layer genes, per ancestry.** EAS: the top signal is *PGM1*
(#1, q = 6.4×10⁻²⁴, expression driver) — placental
phosphoglucomutase activity is long established
([Fazi et al. 1990](https://doi.org/10.1080/00327489008050198)) and PGM1
loss disrupts cellular energy homeostasis
([Conte et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms24098247)), relevant to
placental glycogen handling in diabetic pregnancy
([Lafta et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.28969/ijeir.v10.i2.r3)); followed by
an uncharacterized lncRNA (*ENSG00000290199*, #2, q = 3.4×10⁻²²) — a novel
candidate with no annotation; *PSCA* (#3, alt_polyA driver) —
overexpressed in gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
([Feng et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2559.2007.02925.x));
*FBLN1* (#4, isoform-expression driver) — fibulin-1 functions in placentation
([Singh et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.placenta.2005.10.009)),
placental ECM remodeling in late-onset preeclampsia
([García-Montero et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.3390/medsci14030364)),
and maternal plasma fibulin-1 tracking pregnancy progression
([Orvik et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12884-021-04110-y)); *IQCG*
(#5, expression driver) — ciliary/flagellar function with no prior
placental association (novel candidate); *THNSL2* (#7, expression driver) —
no prior placental association (novel candidate); *RPS28* (#8, expression
driver) — small-subunit ribosomal protein with no prior
placental association (novel candidate); *SPSB2* (#9, expression driver) — an
E3-ligase adaptor targeting iNOS for proteasomal degradation
([Kuang et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1083/jcb.200912087);
[Li et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.niox.2021.04.004)), placing it
in nitric-oxide biology central to placental vascular function;
*TOR1AIP1* (#10,
isoform-expression driver) — the LAP1 nuclear-envelope protein; biallelic
loss causes multisystemic nuclear envelopathy with growth retardation
([Fichtman et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-08493-7);
reviewed in [Mackels et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms24086911)),
with no prior placental association; *CPVL* (#11, expression driver) — a
macrophage serine carboxypeptidase
([Mahoney et al. 2001](https://doi.org/10.1006/geno.2000.6484)) with no
prior placental association (novel candidate); *MRPL43*
(#12, intron-retention driver) — a mitoribosomal protein already known to
carry an antagonistic cis-eQTL acting oppositely on transcription and
translation
([Han & Lee 2022](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12863-022-01057-7)), and fellow
mitoribosomal subunit *MRPL13* drives trophoblast mitochondrial stress in
early-onset preeclampsia
([Chen et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1093/reprod/xaag016)). EUR: *ERAP1* (#1) and *ERAP2*
(#3) above; *ZSCAN9* (#2, expression driver) — KRAB zinc-finger with no
prior placental association (novel candidate); *CTNND1* (#4, RNA-editing
driver) — p120-catenin is required for trophoblast proliferation and
lineage specification at implantation
([Qin et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1093/biolre/ioae163)) and sits in the
Wnt-regulated invasion program
([Knöfler & Pollheimer 2013](https://doi.org/10.3389/fgene.2013.00190));
*STBD1* (#5, expression driver) — the glycophagy receptor linking glycogen to
selective autophagy
([Zhang et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2402817121);
[Tang et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcp.31078)), a second
glycogen-metabolism hit alongside *PGM1*; *CTSB* (#6, RNA-editing driver) —
cathepsin B, whose serum level is
elevated in preeclampsia and tracks disease severity
([Kim et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-016-4129-3);
[Park et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-020-05478-6)); *APIP* (#7, stability driver) —
an anti-apoptotic Apaf-1 inhibitor protective under hypoxia/ischemia
([Cho et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.1074/jbc.m405747200)) that is also
the methionine-salvage enzyme mtnB
([Mary et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0052877)) — a
plausible hypoxia-response link to placental biology; *MEAK7* (#8,
expression driver) — an
mTORC1-associated protein; trophoblast mTOR signaling controls placental
nutrient transport and fetal growth
([Shao et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2017092118);
[Rosario et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1042/cs20243293)); *ARFGAP3*
(#9, isoform-expression driver) — COPI vesicle-coat assembly at the Golgi
([Kartberg et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1074/jbc.m110.180380)), no prior
placental association; *WDR91* (#10,
expression driver) — a Rab7 effector in endolysosomal trafficking
([Rapiteanu et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1111/tra.12409);
[Ma et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.str.2024.09.023)), no prior
placental association; *GBP3* (#11, isoform-expression driver) — an
interferon-inducible GTPase in cell-autonomous immunity
([Tretina et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.1084/jem.20182031);
[Kirkby et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibs.2023.07.002)), no
prior placental association; *RBBP4* (#12, RNA-editing driver) — a
NuRD-complex histone chaperone essential for preimplantation development
([Miao et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1093/biolre/ioaa046)), with NuRD
activity gating trophectoderm fate in ES cells
([Latos et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1242/bio.2012513)) — a plausible
chromatin link to trophoblast lineage control.

**Modality-matched covariates, in line with QTL practice.** Latent-factor
covariates are a standard power lever in QTL mapping
([Stegle et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2011.457)), and
splicing layers — quantified annotation-free from intron usage
([Li et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-017-0004-9)) — have
hidden structure that need not track gene expression. The per-modality HCP
choice behaved as that practice predicts: EUR splicing was null under
expression-derived factors and recovers
`r n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EUR" & n_eg_mod$modality == "splicing"]`
eGenes at its own modality-matched k\*, while the EAS splicing null is flat
across the entire k grid, excluding covariate specification as its cause.

Sub-threshold top-ranked genes (tables above) remain prioritization hints
only`r if (any(mac_tab$n_lt5 > 0)) " — and the flagged low-carrier rows should be discounted outright" else ""`.

# Limitations and next steps

1. **Power.** n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`/`r n_samp["EUR"]` with a ~12k-gene
   testing burden detects only r² ≳ 0.10 (EAS) / 0.19 (EUR) effects.
   Doubling n would roughly halve the detectable r²; matching PANTRY's
   n = 445 would bring the floor to ≈ 0.06. Adding the remaining cohorts and
   the AFR/AMR/SAS strata is the highest-value next step.
2. **EAS splicing is near-null.** The layer yields a handful of FDR ≤ 5%
   eGenes while EUR splicing — at a higher detection floor — yields
   `r n_eg_mod$n[n_eg_mod$ancestry == "EUR" & n_eg_mod$modality == "splicing"]`.
   The EAS result is robust to HCP count (flat k-grid), so covariate
   specification is excluded as the cause; the leading candidate is
   cross-cohort heterogeneity in junction-level quantification (EAS pools
   four cohorts spanning single- and paired-end protocols). Revisiting
   splicing quantification harmonization across the EAS cohorts, and adding
   EAS cohorts, are the targeted next steps.
3. **Technical replicates.** 25 mapped individuals (4 EAS, 21 EUR) have two
   RNA-seq runs. Phenotype values come from the single ComBat-processed run
   per individual, while run-level covariates (cell-type fractions, QC
   metrics) are averaged across the pair — a slight phenotype/covariate
   misalignment for those individuals. Future runs will collapse replicates
   at the count level before batch correction so phenotypes and covariates
   are averaged consistently, with a pre-collapse replicate-concordance QC
   gate.
4. **Carrier-count propagation.** `r if (all(mac_tab$n_lt5 == 0)) "The MAC ≥ 5 floor propagated cleanly to every mapping output (audit table above)." else "The MAC ≥ 5 floor predates outlier exclusion, so low-carrier tests persist in some mapping outputs (audit table above). No reported result depends on them; hit lists should post-filter to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source."`
5. **Ancestry asymmetry.** EUR tests more phenotypes than EAS in every
   modality (ancestry-specific filtering), so cross-ancestry comparisons are
   restricted to genes tested in both.
6. **No pooled cross-ancestry inference** was performed. If combined
   discovery is wanted later, Fisher/Stouffer or an inverse-variance slope
   meta-analysis are the clean options.
7. **Stepwise secondary signals**: `r if (n_secondary == 0) "none called in any layer." else sprintf("%s units carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (table above).", format(n_secondary, big.mark = ','))`
8. **Fine-mapping is in progress; colocalization is future work.** The
   phenotype-level discovery set (ungrouped layer + expression) is being
   fine-mapped jointly across ancestries with SuSHiE (modules 31–34;
   per-variant PIPs, 95% credible sets, cross-ancestry effect correlations,
   and functional-annotation enrichment of high-PIP variants) — results are
   reported separately (`report_finemap`). GWAS colocalization
   (coloc/eCAVIAR) against placental and pregnancy-outcome GWAS and
   locus-zoom visual QC of each hit remain the next steps after
   fine-mapping.
9. **Replication path**: the FDR-significant hits are the priorities for
   lookup in larger placental resources or a future meta-analysis; visual QC
   of phenotype levels by genotype is the immediate sanity check for each.

# Reproducibility

- Results: tensorQTL cis mapping (grouped / ungrouped / combined layers,
  each with stepwise `cis.map_independent` scans), MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5 at
  the genotype intersection, ±1 Mb window, **Storey
  q-values** on pval_beta via the R `qvalue` package (singularity-R bridge).
  Covariates: as described (first-5 PCs + HCP_1–k\* + sex/GA/cell types;
  maternal fraction excluded before correlation pruning; no cap). Genotype
  PCs: cohort-only plink2 PCA on LD-pruned variants.
- Fine-mapping: SuSHiE joint cross-ancestry fine-mapping of the
  FDR-significant phenotype-level discovery set (ungrouped layer; expression
  from the primary scan), with fastVEP/cCRE/open-chromatin enrichment of
  high-PIP variants (scripts 31–34).
- Pipeline scripts: this repository (`05_qtl_mapping/`, scripts 19–35 +
  `compute_qvalues.R`; genotype pooling in `01_genotype_imputation/`).
- Report extras: targeted cross-ancestry/cross-modality lookups, showcase
  locus scans, lead-variant annotations, and gnomAD constraint tables
  (`05_qtl_mapping/35_extract_report_extras.py`), staged into the archive
  under `data/extras/` by `make_report_archive.sh`; report panels that use
  them render only when the corresponding file is present.
- Report code: `report_placenta_xqtl.Rmd` + `xqtl_report_functions.R`;
  figures in `figures/`, tables in `tables/`.
- Gene symbols: `gene_map.tsv` regenerated in full from the normalized GTF
  (config `normalized_gtf`) by `make_report_archive.sh` at archive time —
  covers every tested gene, version-stripped IDs.
